title.zh: 卷三百四十七 列傳第一百〇六 孫鼛 吳時 李昭玘 吳師禮 王漢之 黃廉 朱服 張舜民 盛陶 章衡 顏復 孫升 韓川 龔鼎臣 鄭穆 席旦 喬執中
title.en: Volume 347 Biographies 106: Sun Gao, Wu Shi, Li Zhaoqi, Wu Shili, Wang Hanzhi, Huang Lian, Zhu Fu, Zhang Shunmin, Cheng Tao, Zhang Heng, Yan Fu, Sun Sheng, Han Chuan, Gong Dingchen, Zheng Mu, Xi Dan, Qiao Zhizhong
title.raw: 卷三百四十七 列傳第一百〇六 孫鼛 吳時 李昭玘 吳師禮 王漢之 黃廉 朱服 張舜民 盛陶 章衡 顏復 孫升 韓川 龔鼎臣 鄭穆 席旦 喬執中 Volume 347 Biographies 106: Sun Gao, Wu Shi, Li Zhaoqi, Wu Shili, Wang Hanzhi, Huang Lian, Zhu Fu, Zhang Shunmin, Cheng Tao, Zhang Heng, Yan Fu, Sun Sheng, Han Chuan, Gong Dingchen, Zheng Mu, Xi Dan, Qiao Zhizhong

sentences.zh: 孫鼛，字叔靜，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Sun Gao, style name Shujing, was a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gao, courtesy name Shujing, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 父直官，徙揚之江都。

translations.literal: His father Zhi held office; the family moved to Jiangdu in Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father, surnamed Zhi, served in office and later relocated to Jiangdu in Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鼛年十五，遊太學，蘇洵、滕甫稱之。

translations.literal: At age fifteen Gao entered the Imperial University; Su Xun and Teng Fu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao was fifteen he entered the Imperial University, where Su Xun and Teng Fu spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 用父任，調武平尉，捕獲名盜數十，謝賞不受。

translations.literal: Using his father's privilege, he was appointed Commandant of Wuping, captured several tens of notorious bandits, and declined reward, refusing to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's yin privilege he was appointed commandant of Wuping, where he captured dozens of notorious bandits but refused any reward offered him.

sentences.zh: 再調越州司法參軍，守趙抃薦其材。

translations.literal: Transferred again to judicial military aide in Yue Prefecture; the prefect Zhao Bian recommended his ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was next assigned as judicial aide in Yue Prefecture, and the prefect Zhao Bian commended his abilities.

sentences.zh: 知偃師縣，蒲中優人詭僧服隱民間，以不語惑眾，相傳有異法，奔湊其門。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Yanshi County, actors from Pu in monk's garb feigned and hid among the people, beguiling the crowd by not speaking, with talk passing around of strange methods, rushing to gather at their gate.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Yanshi, he found that entertainers from the Pu region were dressing as monks and living among the populace, mesmerizing crowds with vows of silence and rumors of supernatural powers until people thronged their doors.

sentences.zh: 鼛收按姦狀，立伏辜。

translations.literal: Gao investigated and pressed the criminal facts; they immediately submitted to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Gao investigated the case, uncovered the fraud, and swiftly brought the culprits to justice.

sentences.zh: 韓縝鎮長安，辟入府；

translations.literal: Han Zong was stationed at Chang'an and recruited him into the administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Zong served as military commissioner at Chang'an, he brought Gao onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 縝去，後來者仍挽之使留，居五年，簽書西川判官。

translations.literal: When Zong left, the one who came after still held him back to make him stay; he dwelt five years, then was Recorder of the West Sichuan circuit judge.
translations.idiomatic: Though Han Zong departed, his successor pressed Gao to remain; he stayed five years before being appointed recorder under the West Sichuan judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 或薦於朝，召對，擢提舉廣東常平。

translations.literal: Someone recommended him at court; he was summoned for audience and promoted to intendant of the Guangdong Ever-Normal Granary circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation to the court he was called for an imperial audience and promoted to intendant of the Guangdong Ever-Normal Granary circuit.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初，徙兩浙。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huizong, he was transferred to the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huizong reign he was transferred to the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 由福建轉運判官召為屯田員外。

translations.literal: From Fujian transport vice-commissioner he was summoned as Clerk of Works in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned from the post of Fujian transport vice-commissioner to become Clerk of Works in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 鼛微時與蔡京善，常曰：「蔡子，貴人也；

translations.literal: When Gao was young he was on good terms with Cai Jing, often saying: "Young Cai is a man of nobility;
translations.idiomatic: In his younger days Gao was close to Cai Jing and often remarked, "Cai is destined for greatness;

sentences.zh: 然才不勝德，恐貽天下憂。」

translations.literal: yet his talent does not overcome his virtue; I fear he will bring worry to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: but his talent outstrips his character, and I fear he will bring calamity upon the empire."

sentences.zh: 至是，京還朝，遇諸塗。

translations.literal: At this time Jing returned to court and met him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: By then Cai Jing was returning to the capital and they met on the road.

sentences.zh: 既見，京逆謂曰：「我若用於天子，願助我。」

translations.literal: Once they had met, Jing said in advance: "If I am used by the Son of Heaven, I hope you will help me.
translations.idiomatic: After they greeted each other, Cai said, "If the emperor employs me, I want your help."

sentences.zh: 鼛曰：「公誠能謹守祖宗之法，以正論輔人主，示節儉以先百吏，而絕口不言兵，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Gao said: "Sir, if you can truly carefully guard the laws of the ancestors, with correct discourse assist the sovereign, display thrift to lead the hundred officials ahead, and cut off speech never speaking of war, the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Gao replied, "If you would truly uphold the ancestral statutes, counsel the sovereign with honest principle, set an example of frugality for all the officials, and never breathe a word about war, the realm would be blessed indeed.

sentences.zh: 鼛何為者。」

translations.literal: What would Gao do?
translations.idiomatic: As for me, what could I possibly do for you?"

sentences.zh: 京默然。

translations.literal: Jing was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Cai fell silent.

sentences.zh: 既相，出提點江東刑獄。

translations.literal: Once [Jing] became chancellor, [Gao] went out as judicial intendant of Jiang East.
translations.idiomatic: After Cai became chief councillor, Gao was sent out as judicial intendant for Jiang East circuit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為少府少監、戶部郎中。

translations.literal: Before long he entered service as Assistant Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Bureau Director of Households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed assistant director of the Palace Domestic Service and bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 縣官用度無藝，鼛與尚書曾孝廣、侍郎許幾謀曰：「日增一日，歲增一歲，天下之財豈能給哉？」

translations.literal: State expenditures were without limit; Gao with Minister Zeng Xiaoguang and Vice Minister Xu Ji schemed, saying: "Day adds to day, year adds to year—can the realm's wealth supply it?"
translations.idiomatic: Government spending knew no bounds; Gao met with Minister Zeng Xiaoguang and Vice Minister Xu Ji and said, "Costs rise day by day and year by year—how can the empire's resources keep pace?"

sentences.zh: 共疏論之。

translations.literal: Together they memorialized to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Together they submitted a memorial on the matter.

sentences.zh: 當國者不樂，孝廣、幾由是罷，徙鼛開封。

translations.literal: Those in power were displeased; Xiaoguang and Ji were dismissed on this account, and Gao was transferred to Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: The men then in power took offense; Xiaoguang and Ji lost their posts over it, and Gao was moved to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 遷太僕卿、殿中少監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Court of the Imperial Stud Master and Palace Domestic Service Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to master of the Court of the Imperial Stud and assistant director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 四輔建，以顯謨閣待制知曹州。

translations.literal: When the Four Assistants were established, he was made Xianmo Hall Attendant Reader-in-waiting and prefect of Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Four Assistants were installed, he was made attendant reader-in-waiting at the Xianmo Hall and appointed prefect of Cao.

sentences.zh: 論經始規畫之勞，轉太中大夫，徙鄆州。

translations.literal: Citing merit in initial planning and labor, he was promoted to Grandee of the Palace and transferred to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his work in founding and planning, he was promoted to Grandee of the Palace and transferred to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 邑人子為「草祭」之謠，指切蔡京。

translations.literal: Local youths composed a "grass worship" song, pointing and cutting at Cai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Local youths composed a satirical song called "Grass Sacrifice" that mocked Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 鼛以聞，京怒，使言者誣以它謗，提舉鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: Gao reported it; Jing was angry and had memorialists falsely accuse him of other slander; [Gao was made] intendant of Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gao reported the matter; Cai Jing was furious and had critics fabricate other charges against him, and Gao was relegated to intendant of Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 起知單州，遂致仕。

translations.literal: He was reinstated to govern Dan Prefecture, then retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled to serve as prefect of Dan, then retired from office.

sentences.zh: 靖康二年卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Jingkang, aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Jingkang era, at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈銀青光祿大夫，諡曰「通靖」。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Silver-Green Glory Grandee of Glory; posthumous name "Tongjing."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Silver-Green Glory Grandee of Glory, with the posthumous name Tongjing (Comprehensive Tranquility).

sentences.zh: 鼛篤於行義，在廣東時，蘇軾謫居惠州，極意與周旋。

translations.literal: Gao was steadfast in conduct and righteousness; while in Guangdong, Su Shi was banished to Huizhou, and he exerted his utmost in associating with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was deeply committed to integrity; while serving in Guangdong he went to great lengths to befriend Su Shi, who had been exiled to Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 二子娶晁補之、黃庭堅女，黨事起，家人危懼，鼛一無所顧。

translations.literal: His two sons married daughters of Chao Buzhi and Huang Tingjian; when faction affairs arose, family members were in peril and fear, yet Gao showed not the slightest concern.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons married daughters of Chao Buzhi and Huang Tingjian; when the faction prosecutions began and his household trembled with fear, Gao did not waver in the least.

sentences.zh: 時人稱之。

translations.literal: People of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 吳時，字伸道，邛州人。

translations.literal: Wu Shi, style name Shendao, was a man of Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shi, courtesy name Shendao, was from Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初舉進士，得學究出身；

translations.literal: At first he passed the jinshi examination and received xueju status;
translations.idiomatic: On his first attempt at the jinshi examination he passed with only the lower xueju degree;

sentences.zh: 再試，中甲科。

translations.literal: on a second attempt he placed in the first class.
translations.idiomatic: on a second attempt he ranked in the top class.

sentences.zh: 知華州鄭縣，轉運使檄州餫米五萬輸長安，鄭獨當三萬，時貽書使者曰：「會三萬斛之費，以車則千五百乘，以卒則五萬夫，縣民可役者才二百五十八戶耳。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture, the transport commissioner ordered the prefecture to forward fifty thousand piculs of grain to Chang'an; Zheng alone was to supply thirty thousand. Shi sent a letter to the envoy, saying: "Meeting the cost of thirty thousand piculs, in carts that would be fifteen hundred loads, in laborers fifty thousand men—the county households available for corvée are only two hundred fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture, he received an order from the transport commissioner to send fifty thousand piculs of grain to Chang'an, with Zheng County alone responsible for thirty thousand. Shi wrote to the envoy: "Thirty thousand piculs would require some fifteen hundred cartloads and fifty thousand laborers—yet the county has only two hundred fifty-eight households fit for corvée service.

sentences.zh: 古者用師則贏糧以養兵，無事則移兵以就食，誠能移兵於華，則前費可免。

translations.literal: In antiquity when employing armies one carried surplus grain to feed troops; when there was no affair one moved troops to where food was—if troops could truly be moved to Hua, the prior expense could be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity armies carried extra grain when campaigning and shifted troops to food supplies in peacetime; if troops were stationed at Hua instead, this entire burden could be lifted.

sentences.zh: 華、雍相去百六十里，一旦欲用，朝發而夕至矣。」

translations.literal: Hua and Yong are one hundred sixty li apart; if one wished to use them on a single day, setting out in the morning one would arrive by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Hua and Yong are only one hundred sixty li apart, so forces could march out in the morning and arrive by evening whenever needed.

sentences.zh: 使者從其言。

translations.literal: The envoy followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 陸師閔幹秦、蜀茶馬，辟為屬。

translations.literal: Lu Shimin managed Qin and Shu tea and horses and recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shimin, commissioner of the Qin-Shu Tea and Horse Agency, recruited him as a staff member.

sentences.zh: 章楶欲以御史薦，力辭之，徽宗求言，遠臣上章，封識多不能如式，有司悉卻之，時建言，乃得達。

translations.literal: Zhang Shu wished to recommend him as censor; he forcefully declined. When Huizong sought advice, distant officials submitted memorials; seals and markings often did not conform to regulations, and the relevant offices all rejected them—yet Shi's memorial was able to reach [the throne].
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu wanted to recommend him as censor, but he firmly declined. When Emperor Huizong solicited opinions, memorials from distant officials were often rejected because their seals did not meet format requirements; Shi's submission alone got through.

sentences.zh: 為睦親宅教授，提舉永興軍路學事。

translations.literal: He became professor at the Court of Kinship Lodge and intendant of educational affairs for the Yongxing Military Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as professor at the Court of Kinship Lodge and as intendant of schools for the Yongxing Military Circuit.

sentences.zh: 華州諸生有觸忌諱者，教授欲上之，曰：「是間言語，皆臣子所不忍聞。」

translations.literal: Among Hua Prefecture students there were some who violated taboos; the professor wished to report them upward. [Shi] said: "These words in between are what ministers and sons cannot bear to hear.
translations.idiomatic: When some students in Hua Prefecture used language that violated taboo, the professor wanted to report them. Shi said, "Such language is what a loyal subject cannot bear even to hear.

sentences.zh: 時即火其書，曰：「臣子不忍聞，而令君父聞乎？」

translations.literal: Shi immediately burned the book, saying: "If ministers and sons cannot bear to hear it, shall we let the sovereign and father hear it?"
translations.idiomatic: He at once burned the documents and said, "If we cannot bear to hear it, how can we allow our ruler and father to hear it?"

sentences.zh: 召為工部員外郎，改禮部，兼辟雍司業。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Bureau Director of Works, transferred to Rites, and concurrently Director of Studies at the Piyong Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as bureau director in the Ministry of Works, then moved to the Ministry of Rites while also serving as director of studies at the Piyong Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 大觀興算學，議以黃帝為先師。

translations.literal: In the Daguan era the mathematics academy was established; there was discussion of making the Yellow Emperor the chief teacher.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daguan period a school of mathematics was founded, and officials debated making the Yellow Emperor its chief teacher.

sentences.zh: 時言：「今祠祀聖祖，祝板書臣名，而釋奠孔子，但列中祀。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Now in sacrificing to the sacred ancestor, prayer boards inscribe the subject's name, yet in the libation to Confucius he is only listed among mid-grade sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Shi argued: "In rites to the sacred ancestor our names appear on the prayer boards, yet Confucius receives only a mid-grade offering.

sentences.zh: 數學，六藝之一耳，當以何禮事之？」

translations.literal: Mathematics is only one of the Six Arts—by what rite should it be served?"
translations.idiomatic: Mathematics is but one of the Six Arts—what ceremony could possibly elevate it above that?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 遷太僕少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 張商英罷相，言者指時為黨，出知耀州，又降通判鼎州；

translations.literal: When Zhang Shangying left as chancellor, memorialists pointed to Shi as a partisan; he was sent out to govern Yao Prefecture, then demoted to vice-prefect of Ding Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Shangying was dismissed as chancellor, critics denounced Shi as a factionalist; he was sent to govern Yao Prefecture and then demoted to vice-prefect of Ding;

sentences.zh: 未赴，提舉河東常平。

translations.literal: before he took up the post he was made intendant of the Hedong Ever-Normal Granary circuit.
translations.idiomatic: before he could take up the latter post he was appointed intendant of the Hedong Ever-Normal Granary circuit.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，發公粟以振民。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he distributed public grain to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he opened government granaries to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 童貫經略北方，每訪以邊事，輒不答。

translations.literal: Tong Guan managed the northern frontier; each time he visited and asked about border affairs, Shi always would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan, commissioner of the northern frontier, repeatedly questioned him about border affairs, but Shi refused to reply.

sentences.zh: 還為大晟典樂，擢中書舍人、給事中。

translations.literal: He returned as director of music for the Da Sheng Bureau and was promoted to Secretariat Drafter and Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to head music at the Da Sheng Bureau and was promoted to secretariat drafter and chief supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 內侍何欣謫監衡州酒，猶領節度使，時奏奪之。

translations.literal: The inner attendant He Xin was demoted to supervise the Hengzhou wine monopoly yet still held the title of military commissioner; Shi memorialized to strip it from him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch He Xin, though demoted to supervise the Hengzhou wine monopoly, still retained his military commissioner title; Shi submitted a memorial to revoke it.

sentences.zh: 又因進對及取燕事，曰：「祖宗盟血未乾，渝之必速亂。」

translations.literal: Again, in presenting himself at audience he spoke of the campaign to take Yan, saying: "The ancestral covenant's blood is not yet dry—violating it will quickly bring chaos.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, during an audience on the Yan campaign, he said, "The blood of our ancestors' covenant has scarcely dried—to break it will bring swift ruin.

sentences.zh: 蔡攸聞之，以告王黼，黼怒，斥為腐儒。

translations.literal: Cai You heard of it and told Wang Fu; Fu was angry and called him a rotten Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You heard of this and informed Wang Fu, who in fury dismissed him as a pedantic hack.

sentences.zh: 時求去，以徽猷閣待制兼侍讀，俄提舉上請太平宮。

translations.literal: Shi sought leave and was made Huiyou Hall Attendant Reader and Lecturer; soon he was intendant of the Shangqing Taiping Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shi asked to leave office and was made attendant reader and lecturer at the Huiyou Hall; shortly afterward he became intendant of the Shangqing Taiping Palace.

sentences.zh: 西歸，遇其里人趙雍，為言：「取燕必召禍。

translations.literal: Returning west, he met his fellow townsman Zhao Yong and told him: "Taking Yan will certainly summon disaster.
translations.idiomatic: On his way home to the west he met his townsman Zhao Yong and said, "The seizure of Yan is sure to bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 吾老，得不遭其變，幸矣。」

translations.literal: I am old; to escape suffering its upheaval—fortunate indeed."
translations.idiomatic: I am old now; if I can die without living through that calamity, I shall count myself lucky."

sentences.zh: 累歲而卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: Several years later he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died a few years later, at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 時敏於為文，未嘗屬稿，落筆已就，兩學目之曰：「立地書廚。」

translations.literal: Shi was sharp in composing writing; he never drafted outlines, and putting brush to paper the work was already done. The two academies called him "the standing book cupboard."
translations.idiomatic: Shi wrote with extraordinary speed, never outlining a draft beforehand; the moment his brush touched paper the essay was complete. Students at both imperial academies nicknamed him "the walking library."

sentences.zh: 李昭玘

translations.literal: Li Zhaoqi
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhaoqi

sentences.zh: 李昭玘，字成季，濟南人。

translations.literal: Li Zhaoqi, style name Chenji, was a man of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhaoqi, courtesy name Chenji, was from Jinan.

sentences.zh: 少與晁補之齊名，為蘇軾所知。

translations.literal: In youth he was equally famed with Chao Buzhi and was known to Su Shi.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he enjoyed equal renown with Chao Buzhi and won the notice of Su Shi.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，徐州教授。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi degree and became professor at Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After earning his jinshi degree he served as professor at Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 守孫覺深禮之，每從容講學及古人行己處世之要，相得歡甚。

translations.literal: The prefect Sun Jue deeply honored him; they would at leisure discuss learning and the essentials of how ancients conducted themselves and dealt with the world, getting on in great delight.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Sun Jue treated him with great respect; they often spent leisurely hours discussing scholarship and the principles by which the ancients ordered their lives, and the two became fast friends.

sentences.zh: 用李清臣薦，為秘書省正字、校書郎，加秘閣校理。

translations.literal: On Li Qingchen's recommendation he became Rectifier of Texts in the Secretariat and collating secretary, then added as collator of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Li Qingchen he was appointed rectifier of texts and collating secretary in the Secretariat, then collator of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 通判潞州，潞民死多不葬，昭玘斥官地，畫兆竁，具棺衾，作文風曉之，俗為一變。

translations.literal: As vice-prefect of Lu Prefecture, many of the people of Lu died without burial; Zhaoqi set aside official land, marked grave plots, provided coffins and shrouds, and wrote an essay on custom to instruct them—the practice was wholly changed.
translations.idiomatic: As vice-prefect of Lu he found that many locals were left unburied; he allocated government land, marked grave sites, supplied coffins and shrouds, and wrote an exhortation on burial customs that transformed local practice entirely.

sentences.zh: 入為秘書丞、開封推官，俄提點永興、京西、京東路刑獄，坐元符黨奪官。

translations.literal: He entered as Secretariat Director and Kaifeng investigating censor; soon he was judicial intendant for Yongxing, Jingxi, and Jingdong circuits, and lost his post for involvement in the Yuanfu faction list.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Secretariat and investigating censor in Kaifeng, then soon made judicial intendant for the Yongxing, Jingxi, and Jingdong circuits; he was stripped of office for Yuanfu faction association.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，召為右司員外郎，遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended, he was summoned as Bureau Director of the Right Office and promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong came to the throne he was recalled as bureau director of the right office and promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 韓忠彥欲用為起居舍人，曾布持之，布使山陵，命始下。

translations.literal: Han Zhongyan wished to employ him as Attendant Gentleman of the Household; Zeng Bu held it up; when Bu went on the mountain tomb mission the order was finally issued.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhongyan wanted to appoint him attendant gentleman of the household, but Zeng Bu blocked the appointment until Bu departed for the imperial tomb rites, when the order finally went out.

sentences.zh: 為陳次升所論，出知滄州。

translations.literal: He was attacked by Chen Cisheng and sent out to govern Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Cisheng impeached him, and he was sent out as prefect of Cang.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，詔以昭玘嘗傾搖先烈，每改元豐敕條，倡從寬之邪說，罷主管鴻慶宮，遂入黨籍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning, an edict stated that Zhaoqi had once shaken the achievements of the former sovereigns, altering Yuanfeng edicts each time and advocating perverse doctrines of leniency; he was dismissed from supervising Hongqing Palace and entered the faction register.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongning era an edict charged that Zhaoqi had undermined the accomplishments of the previous reign, repeatedly revising Yuanfeng statutes and preaching lax heterodoxies; he was removed from supervising Hongqing Palace and entered the proscribed faction list.

sentences.zh: 居閑十五年，自號「樂靜先生」。

translations.literal: He lived in retirement fifteen years and styled himself "Master Lejing" (Delighting in Stillness).
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for fifteen years and took the sobriquet Master Lejing (Delighting in Stillness).

sentences.zh: 寓意法書、圖畫，貯於十囊，命曰「燕遊十友」，為之序，以為：「與今之人友，或趨附而陷於禍，吾寧與十者友，久益有味也。」

translations.literal: He invested his interest in model calligraphy and paintings, stored them in ten pouches, and named them the "Ten Friends of the Swallow Tour"; he wrote a preface for them, saying: "Befriending people of today, one may fawn and fall into disaster; I would rather befriend these ten—over time the flavor grows richer."
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to fine calligraphy and painting, kept them in ten cases he called the "Ten Companions of the Swallow Excursion," and wrote a preface declaring: "Friendship with men of the present often means flattery and ruin; I prefer these ten companions, whose company grows richer with time."

sentences.zh: 初，昭玘校試高密，得侯蒙。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhaoqi examined candidates at Gaomi, he obtained Hou Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while grading examinations at Gaomi, Zhaoqi had passed Hou Meng.

sentences.zh: 蒙執政，思顧舊恩，使人致己意，昭玘唯求秘閣法帖而已。

translations.literal: When Meng took power he thought to repay old kindness and sent someone to convey his intent; Zhaoqi asked only for Secret Archive model calligraphy rubbings.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Meng rose to power he wished to repay the old debt and sent an emissary with his offer; Zhaoqi asked only for rubbings from the Secret Archive collection.

sentences.zh: 使陝西時，延安小將車吉者被誣為盜，昭玘察知無它。

translations.literal: When he was on mission in Shaanxi, a young officer of Yan'an named Che Ji was falsely accused of banditry; Zhaoqi investigated and knew there was nothing else to it.
translations.idiomatic: While on duty in Shaanxi, a young Yan'an officer named Che Ji was falsely accused of robbery; Zhaoqi looked into the case and found no other wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 吉後立戰功，至皇城使，遇昭玘京師，拜於前曰：「感公生存之恩，願以名馬為獻。」

translations.literal: Later Ji won military merit and rose to Commissioner of the Imperial City; meeting Zhaoqi in the capital, he bowed before him and said: "I am grateful for your grace in preserving my life and wish to present a famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: Ji later distinguished himself in battle and rose to commissioner of the imperial city; encountering Zhaoqi in the capital, he bowed and said, "I owe you my life and wish to offer you a fine steed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 笑卻之。

translations.literal: He smiled and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoqi smiled and refused.

sentences.zh: 晚知歙州，辭不行。

translations.literal: In his later years he was appointed prefect of She Prefecture but declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he was appointed prefect of She but declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，復以起居舍人召，而已卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang he was again summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Household, but he had already died.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingkang era he was again summoned as attendant gentleman of the household, but he had already died.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，追復直徽猷閣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing, his post as Direct Attendant of the Huiyou Hall was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing era his rank as direct attendant of the Huiyou Hall was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 吳師禮

translations.literal: Wu Shili
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shili

sentences.zh: 吳師禮，字安仲，杭州錢塘人。

translations.literal: Wu Shili, style name Anzhong, was a man of Qiantang in Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shili, courtesy name Anzhong, was from Qiantang in Hang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太學上舍賜第，調涇縣主簿，知天長縣。

translations.literal: Granted rank as upper-house graduate of the Imperial University, he was appointed chief clerk of Jing County and then magistrate of Tianchang County.
translations.idiomatic: After graduating at the top of the Imperial University's upper division he was appointed chief clerk of Jing County and later magistrate of Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 召太學博士、秘書省正字，預餞鄒浩，免。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Imperial University erudite and Rectifier of Texts in the Secretariat; because he attended the farewell feast for Zou Hao he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to serve as erudite of the Imperial University and rectifier of texts in the Secretariat, but was dismissed for having attended the farewell banquet for Zou Hao.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初，為開封府推官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huizong he served as investigating censor in the Kaifeng prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huizong reign he served as investigating censor in the Kaifeng metropolitan office.

sentences.zh: 蔡王似宮吏有不順語，下之府，師禮主治。

translations.literal: Palace attendants of Prince Cai had used disrespectful language; the case was sent down to the prefectural office and Shili took chief charge of the trial.
translations.idiomatic: When attendants of Prince Cai used seditious language, the case was referred to Kaifeng and Shili presided over the investigation.

sentences.zh: 獄成，不使一詞及王；

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, not a single word implicated the prince;
translations.idiomatic: When the trial concluded, not one statement implicated the prince;

sentences.zh: 吏雖有死者，亦不被以指斥罪。

translations.literal: even though some attendants died, they were not charged with crimes of direct accusation.
translations.idiomatic: and even attendants who were executed were not convicted of crimes that named him.

sentences.zh: 擢右司諫，改右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Remonstrator of the Right Office and then Bureau Director of the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to remonstrator of the right office and then bureau director of the right office.

sentences.zh: 師禮工翰墨，帝嘗訪以字學，對曰：「陛下御極之初，當志其大者，臣不敢以末伎對。」

translations.literal: Shili was skilled in calligraphy and brushwork; the emperor once consulted him on the study of characters. He replied: "At the beginning of Your Majesty's accession you should set your mind on great affairs; your servant dare not answer with petty craft.
translations.idiomatic: Shili excelled at calligraphy; the emperor once asked his views on paleography. He answered, "At the start of your reign Your Majesty should fix your mind on great matters; I dare not reply with a trifling art.

sentences.zh: 聞者獎其得體。

translations.literal: Hearers praised his appropriateness.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers praised his tact.

sentences.zh: 以直秘閣知宿州，卒。

translations.literal: As Direct Attendant of the Secret Archive he governed Su Prefecture and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed direct attendant of the Secret Archive and prefect of Su, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 師禮遊太學時，兄師仁為正，守《春秋》學。

translations.literal: When Shili was at the Imperial University, his elder brother Shiren was Director, upholding the study of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: While Shili was studying at the Imperial University, his elder brother Shiren served as Director and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 它學官有惡之者，條其疑問諸生，師禮悉以兄說對。

translations.literal: Among the other university instructors were those who hated him; they listed doubtful points to query the students, and Shili answered them all with his brother's explanations.
translations.idiomatic: Some of the other instructors bore him ill will; they set out doubtful points to test the students, and Shili answered every one with his brother's interpretations.

sentences.zh: 學官怒，鳴鼓坐堂上，眾質之，師禮引據《三傳》，意氣自如。

translations.literal: The instructor grew angry, sounded the drum, and seated himself in the hall; the assembly interrogated him, and Shili cited the Three Commentaries, his bearing entirely at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The instructor grew angry, sounded the drum, and took his seat in the hall to interrogate him before the assembly; Shili cited the Three Commentaries in support, as composed as ever.

sentences.zh: 江公望時在旁，心竊喜。

translations.literal: Jiang Gongwang was then at his side and inwardly rejoiced in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gongwang was present and inwardly rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 後相遇於泌陽，公望謂曰：「子異日得志，當如何？」

translations.literal: Later they met again in Biyang; Gongwang said to him, "If you attain your ambition another day, what will you do?"
translations.idiomatic: Later they met again in Biyang; Gongwang said to him, "If you rise to office one day, what will you do?

sentences.zh: 曰：「但為人作豐年耳。」

translations.literal: He said, "Only to make a year of plenty for others."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Only to bring others a year of plenty."

sentences.zh: 遂定交。

translations.literal: Thereupon they formed a friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 師仁，字坦求。

translations.literal: Shiren, styled Tanqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Shiren, styled Tanqiu.

sentences.zh: 篤學厲志，不事科舉。

translations.literal: Deep in learning and firm in purpose, he did not pursue the civil-service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in learning and firm in resolve, he did not pursue the civil-service examinations.

sentences.zh: 喪親，廬墓下，日倩旁寺僧造飯一缽以充饑，不復置庖爨及蓄僮僕。

translations.literal: When his parents died, he built a hut by the tomb; each day he hired monks from a nearby temple to prepare one bowl of food to stave off hunger, and did not again set up a kitchen or keep household servants.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died, he built a mourning hut by the tomb; each day he hired monks from a nearby temple to prepare a single bowl of food to stave off hunger, and kept no kitchen or household servants.

sentences.zh: 郡守陳襄、鄧潤甫、蒲宗孟皆以遺逸薦於朝。

translations.literal: The prefectural administrators Chen Xiang, Deng Runfu, and Pu Zongmeng all recommended him to the court as a recluse of merit.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural administrators Chen Xiang, Deng Runfu, and Pu Zongmeng all recommended him to the court as a recluse of outstanding merit.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，召為太學正，遷博士，十年無它除。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was summoned as Director of the Imperial University, promoted to Erudite, and for ten years received no other appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was summoned as Director of the Imperial University, then promoted to Erudite; for ten years he received no other appointment.

sentences.zh: 後為潁川、吳王宮教授，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as instructor in the princely establishments of Yingchuan and Wu, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as instructor in the princely establishments of Yingchuan and Wu, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 王漢之

translations.literal: Wang Hanzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hanzhi

sentences.zh: 王漢之，字彥昭，衢州常山人。

translations.literal: Wang Hanzhi, styled Yanzhao, was a native of Changshan in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hanzhi, styled Yanzhao, was a native of Changshan in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 父介，舉制科，以直聞，至秘閣校理。

translations.literal: His father Jie passed the decree examination, won renown for integrity, and rose to Collation Editor in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jie passed the decree examination, won renown for integrity, and rose to Collation Editor in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 漢之進士甲科，調秀州司戶參軍，知金華、澠池二縣，為鴻臚丞，知真州。

translations.literal: Hanzhi passed the jinshi in the top tier, was appointed Registrar in the Xiuzhou revenue office, served as magistrate of Jinhua and Mianchi counties, became Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, and governed Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi passed the jinshi in the top tier, was appointed registrar in the Xiuzhou revenue office, served as magistrate of Jinhua and Mianchi counties, became Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, and governed Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 時詔諸道經畫財用上諸朝，漢之言：「所在無都籍，是以不能周知而校其登耗以待用。

translations.literal: When an imperial order directed each circuit to survey fiscal resources and report to the court, Hanzhi said, "Locally there are no unified registers, and so revenues and expenditures cannot be fully known and compared in readiness for use.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial order directed each circuit to survey fiscal resources and report to the court, Hanzhi said, "No unified registers exist locally, and so revenues and expenditures cannot be fully known and compared in readiness for use.

sentences.zh: 願令郡縣先置籍，總之諸道，則天下如指諸掌矣。」

translations.literal: I ask that each prefecture and county be required to maintain registers first, with the circuits aggregating them; then the empire would be like pointing to the palm."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that each prefecture and county be required to maintain registers first, with the circuits aggregating them; then the whole empire would lie in the palm of one's hand."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted this.

sentences.zh: 入為開封府推官，歷工、吏、禮三部員外郎，太常少卿。

translations.literal: He entered court as judicial reviewer in the Kaifeng prefectural office, and served successively as Vice Director in the Ministries of Works, Personnel, and Rites, and as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as judicial reviewer in the Kaifeng prefectural office, and served successively as Vice Director in the Ministries of Works, Personnel, and Rites, and as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 蔡京置講議司。

translations.literal: Cai Jing established the Discussion Office.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing established the Discussion Office.

sentences.zh: 漢之，其客也，引為參詳官。

translations.literal: Hanzhi was his client and was brought in as a consulting official.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi was his client and was brought in as a consulting official.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部侍郎，轉戶部，以顯謨閣待制知瀛州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and with the provisional title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Xianmo Pavilion governed Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and with the provisional title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Xianmo Pavilion governed Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 言：「自何承矩規塘濼之地屯田，東達於海。

translations.literal: He said, "Since He Chengju planned marshland reclamation for garrison farming, extending eastward to the sea,
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Since He Chengju planned marshland reclamation for garrison farming, extending eastward to the sea,

sentences.zh: 其後又修保塞五州為堤道，備種所宜木至三百萬本，此中國萬世之利也。

translations.literal: and later the embankment roads of the five border prefectures of Baosai were repaired, with tree plantings suited to the soil numbering three million—this was a benefit to China for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: and later the embankment roads of the five border prefectures of Baosai were repaired, with tree plantings suited to the soil numbering three million—this was a benefit to China for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 今浸失其道，願講行之。」

translations.literal: Today these works are gradually lost; I ask that they be studied and put back into practice."
translations.idiomatic: Today these works are gradually lost; I ask that they be studied and put back into practice."

sentences.zh: 雄州歸信、容城災，兩輸戶請蠲稅，吏不聽。

translations.literal: In Xiongzhou, Guixin and Rongcheng suffered disaster; dual-tax households requested tax relief, but the clerks refused.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiongzhou, Guixin and Rongcheng suffered disaster; dual-tax households requested tax relief, but the clerks refused.

sentences.zh: 漢之言：「雄州規小利，失大體，萬一契丹蠲之，為朝廷羞。」

translations.literal: Hanzhi said, "Xiongzhou grasps at petty profit and loses sight of the larger principle; should the Khitan grant relief instead, it would shame the court."
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi said, "Xiongzhou grasps at petty profit and loses sight of the larger principle; should the Khitan grant relief instead, it would shame the court."

sentences.zh: 徙江寧、河南府，不至，而為蘇、潭、洪三州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangning and Henan prefectures but did not take up those posts, and instead governed the three prefectures of Suzhou, Tanzhou, and Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiangning and Henan prefectures but did not take up those posts, and instead governed the three prefectures of Suzhou, Tanzhou, and Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 召拜兵部侍郎，復以顯謨閣直學士知成都，又不至，連徙五州，入為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Vice Minister of War, he again received the straight title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Xianmo Pavilion to govern Chengdu but did not go; after successive transfers through five prefectures he entered court as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned and appointed Vice Minister of War, he again received the straight title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Xianmo Pavilion to govern Chengdu but did not go; after successive transfers through five prefectures he entered court as Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，還，言其主不恤民政，而掊克荒淫，亡可跂而待也。

translations.literal: On a mission to the Khitan, upon his return he reported that their ruler neglected civil administration while extorting and indulging in excess, and that their fall was something one could await by standing on tiptoe.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Khitan, upon his return he reported that their ruler neglected civil administration while extorting and indulging in excess, and that their fall was imminent.

sentences.zh: 徽宗悅，以知定州。

translations.literal: Huizong was pleased and appointed him to govern Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong was pleased and appointed him to govern Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙江寧。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was transferred to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was transferred to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 方臘之亂，錄奏報禦捕功，加龍圖閣直學士，又進延康殿學士。

translations.literal: During the Fang La rebellion, his memorials on defense and suppression were rewarded with promotion to Straight Gentleman of the Longtu Pavilion, and again to Gentleman of the Yankang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Fang La rebellion, his memorials on defense and suppression were rewarded with promotion to Straight Gentleman of the Longtu Pavilion, and again to Gentleman of the Yankang Hall.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 弟渙之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Huanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Huanzhi.

sentences.zh: 弟 渙之

translations.literal: Younger Brother Huanzhi
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother Huanzhi

sentences.zh: 渙之，字彥舟。

translations.literal: Huanzhi, styled Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huanzhi, styled Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 未冠，擢上第，有司疑年未及銓格，特補武勝軍節度推官。

translations.literal: Before reaching adulthood he placed at the top of the examinations; the authorities doubted he met the age requirement for assignment, and he was specially appointed as judicial reviewer in the Wusheng circuit military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching adulthood he placed at the top of the examinations; the authorities doubted he met the age requirement for assignment, and he was specially appointed as judicial reviewer in the Wusheng circuit military commission.

sentences.zh: 方新置學官，以為杭州教授，知潁上縣。

translations.literal: When university instructors were newly established, he was made instructor at Hangzhou and magistrate of Yingshang county.
translations.idiomatic: When university instructors were newly established, he was made instructor at Hangzhou and magistrate of Yingshang county.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，為太學博士，校對黃本秘書。

translations.literal: During the Yuanyou era he was an Erudite at the Imperial University and collated the yellow-draft manuscripts of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era he was an Erudite at the Imperial University and collated the yellow-draft manuscripts of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 通判衛州，入編修《兩朝魯衛信錄》。

translations.literal: As acting prefect of Weizhou he entered service to compile the Record of Trust between Lu and Wei of the Two Reigns.
translations.idiomatic: As acting prefect of Weizhou he entered service to compile the Record of Trust between Lu and Wei of the Two Reigns.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，以日食求言。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended the throne, he sought advice on account of a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended the throne, he sought advice on account of a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 渙之用大臣交薦召對，因言：「求言非難，聽之難；

translations.literal: Huanzhi was summoned for audience through senior officials' joint recommendation, and said, "To solicit advice is not difficult; to listen is difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Huanzhi was summoned for audience through senior officials' joint recommendation, and said, "To solicit advice is not difficult; to listen is difficult;

sentences.zh: 聽之非難，察而用之難。

translations.literal: to listen is not difficult; to examine and employ it is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: to listen is not difficult; to examine and employ it is difficult.

sentences.zh: 今國家每下求言之詔，而下之報上，乃或不然，以指陳闕失為訕上，以阿諛佞諂為尊君，以論議趨時為國是，以可否相濟為邪說。

translations.literal: Today, whenever the state issues an edict seeking counsel, the responses from below to above are sometimes otherwise: pointing out faults is taken as deriding the ruler, flattery is taken as honoring the sovereign, debating timely policies is taken as the national consensus, and both sides of an argument are taken as heterodox talk.
translations.idiomatic: Today, whenever the state issues an edict seeking counsel, the responses from below to above are sometimes otherwise: pointing out faults is taken as deriding the ruler, flattery is taken as honoring the sovereign, debating timely policies is taken as the national consensus, and reconciling yes and no is taken as heterodox talk.

sentences.zh: 志士仁人知言之無益也，不復有言，而小人肆為詭譎可駭之論，苟容偷合。

translations.literal: Men of steadfast purpose, knowing that speech is useless, speak no more, while petty men freely advance bizarre and alarming theories, grasping at temporary accommodation.
translations.idiomatic: Men of steadfast purpose, knowing that speech is useless, speak no more, while petty men freely advance bizarre and alarming theories, grasping at temporary accommodation.

sentences.zh: 願陛下虛心公聽，言無逆遜，唯是之從；

translations.literal: I ask Your Majesty to listen with an open mind in the public interest, to accept words without regard to whether they seem contrary, and to follow what is right;
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to listen with an open mind in the public interest, to accept words without regard to whether they seem contrary, and to follow what is right;

sentences.zh: 事無今昔，唯當為貴；

translations.literal: in matters without distinction between past and present, to hold only what ought to be done as precious;
translations.idiomatic: in matters without distinction between past and present, to hold only what ought to be done as precious;

sentences.zh: 人無同異，唯正是用。

translations.literal: among people without distinction of faction, to employ only the upright.
translations.idiomatic: among people without distinction of faction, to employ only the upright.

sentences.zh: 則人心說，治道成，天意得矣。」

translations.literal: Then hearts will be content, governance will succeed, and Heaven's intent will be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Then hearts will be content, governance will succeed, and Heaven's intent will be fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 帝欣然延納，欲任以諫官、御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor received this with pleasure and wished to appoint him remonstrance or censorial official.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received this with pleasure and wished to appoint him remonstrance or censorial official.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「臣由大臣薦，不可以居是官。」

translations.literal: He declined, saying, "I came through senior ministers' recommendation; I cannot accept such an office."
translations.idiomatic: He declined, saying, "I came through senior ministers' recommendation; I cannot accept such an office."

sentences.zh: 乃拜吏部員外郎，遷左司員外郎、起居舍人，擢中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then Vice Director in the Left Office and Drafting Gentleman for Court Audience, and was promoted to Drafting Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then Vice Director in the Left Office and Drafting Gentleman for Court Audience, and was promoted to Drafting Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趨省之日，詞頭三十三，下筆即就。

translations.literal: On the day he attended the Secretariat, there were thirty-three draft titles; he completed them at once.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he attended the Secretariat, there were thirty-three draft titles; he completed them at once.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，進給事中、吏部侍郎，以寶文閣待制知廣州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongning era he was promoted to Chief Supervising Censor and Vice Minister of Personnel, and with the provisional title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Baowen Pavilion governed Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongning era he was promoted to Chief Supervising Censor and Vice Minister of Personnel, and with the provisional title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Baowen Pavilion governed Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 言者論渙之當元祐之末，與陳瓘、龔𡙇、張庭堅遊，既棄於紹聖，而今復之，有害初政。

translations.literal: Critics argued that at the end of Yuanyou Huanzhi had associated with Chen Guan, Gong Shen, and Zhang Tingjian; abandoned in the Shaosheng era, yet now restored—harmful to the inaugural policies.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that at the end of Yuanyou Huanzhi had associated with Chen Guan, Gong Shen, and Zhang Tingjian; cast aside in the Shaosheng era, yet now restored—harmful to the inaugural policies.

sentences.zh: 解職知舒州，入黨籍。

translations.literal: He was removed from office and made prefect of Shuzhou, and entered the faction register.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office and made prefect of Shuzhou, and entered the faction register.

sentences.zh: 尋知福州，未至，復徙廣州。

translations.literal: Soon he was assigned to Fuzhou but before arriving was transferred again to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned to Fuzhou but before arriving was transferred again to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 蕃客殺奴，市舶使據舊比，止送其長杖笞，渙之不可，論如法。

translations.literal: A foreign merchant killed a slave; the maritime trade commissioner, citing precedent, would only send the merchant chief back for bamboo strokes; Huanzhi refused and argued for punishment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign merchant killed a slave; the maritime trade commissioner, citing precedent, would only send the merchant chief back for bamboo strokes; Huanzhi refused and argued for punishment according to law.

sentences.zh: 召詣闕，言者復拾故語以阻之，罷為洪州。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, critics again dredged up old charges to block him, and he was dismissed to govern Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, critics again dredged up old charges to block him, and he was dismissed to govern Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 改滁州，歷潭、杭、揚三州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chuzhou and successively governed Tanzhou, Hangzhou, and Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chuzhou and successively governed Tanzhou, Hangzhou, and Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 張商英相，為給事中、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shangying became chief councillor, Huanzhi was made Chief Supervising Censor and Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shangying became chief councillor, Huanzhi was made Chief Supervising Censor and Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 商英去，亦出守。

translations.literal: When Shangying left office, Huanzhi too was sent out as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Shangying left office, Huanzhi too was sent out as prefect.

sentences.zh: 越八年，知中山府，加寶文閣直學士。

translations.literal: Eight years later he governed Zhongshan prefecture, with addition of the straight title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Baowen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later he governed Zhongshan prefecture, with addition of the straight title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Baowen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議北伐，渙之以疾提舉明道宮。

translations.literal: When the court debated a northern campaign, Huanzhi pleaded illness and was made superintendent of the Mingdao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated a northern campaign, Huanzhi pleaded illness and was made superintendent of the Mingdao Palace.

sentences.zh: 又四年卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: Four years later he died at the age of forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he died at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 渙之性淡泊，恬於仕進，每云：「乘車常以顛墜處之，乘舟常以覆溺處之，仕宦常以不遇處之，則無事矣。」

translations.literal: By nature Huanzhi was detached and indifferent to advancement; he often said, "When riding in a carriage, always imagine overturning; when aboard a boat, always imagine capsizing; in office, always imagine meeting no success—then nothing will trouble you."
translations.idiomatic: By nature Huanzhi was detached and indifferent to advancement; he often said, "When riding in a carriage, imagine overturning; when aboard a boat, imagine capsizing; in office, imagine meeting no success—then nothing will trouble you."

sentences.zh: 其歸趣如此。

translations.literal: Such was the bent of his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the bent of his mind.

sentences.zh: 黃廉，字夷仲，洪州分寧人。

translations.literal: Huang Lian, styled Yizhong, was a native of Fenning in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Lian, styled Yizhong, was a native of Fenning in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，歷州縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and served through prefectural and county posts.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and served through prefectural and county posts.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，或薦之王安石。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining reforms, someone recommended him to Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining reforms, someone recommended him to Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 安石與之言，問免役事，廉據舊法以對，甚悉。

translations.literal: Anshi conversed with him and asked about the labor-exemption law; Lian answered according to the old statutes in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi conversed with him and asked about the labor-exemption law; Lian answered according to the old statutes in full detail.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「是必能辦新法。」

translations.literal: Anshi said, "He will certainly be able to carry out the new laws."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said, "He will certainly be able to carry out the new laws."

sentences.zh: 白神宗，召訪時務，對曰：「陛下意在便民，法非不良也，而吏非其人。

translations.literal: He reported this to Emperor Shenzong, who summoned Lian to inquire about current affairs; he replied, "Your Majesty's intent lies in benefiting the people; the laws are not inherently bad, but the clerks are not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: He reported this to Emperor Shenzong, who summoned Lian to inquire about current affairs; he replied, "Your Majesty's intent lies in benefiting the people; the laws are not inherently bad, but the clerks are not the right men.

sentences.zh: 朝廷立法之意則一，而四方推奉紛然不同，所以法行而民病，陛下不盡察也。

translations.literal: The court's intent in legislating is one, yet implementation differs widely in every quarter; this is why the laws operate while the people suffer illness—Your Majesty does not fully investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The court's intent in legislating is one, yet implementation differs widely in every quarter; this is why the laws operate while the people suffer—Your Majesty does not fully investigate.

sentences.zh: 河朔被水，河南、齊、晉 旱，淮、浙飛蝗，江南疫癘，陛下不盡知也。」

translations.literal: The Hebei has suffered flooding; Henan, Qi, and Jin are in drought; Huai and Zhejiang have locust plagues; Jiangnan has epidemic illness—Your Majesty does not fully know.
translations.idiomatic: The Hebei has suffered flooding; Henan, Qi, and Jin are in drought; Huai and Zhejiang have locust plagues; Jiangnan has epidemic illness—Your Majesty does not fully know.

sentences.zh: 帝即命廉體量振濟東道，除司農丞。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately ordered Lian to survey and provide relief on the eastern circuits, and appointed him Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately ordered Lian to survey and provide relief on the eastern circuits, and appointed him Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 還報合旨，擢利州路轉運判官，復丞司農。

translations.literal: On his return his report accorded with the Emperor's intent; he was promoted to transport assistant of Lizhou circuit, and again served as assistant director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On his return his report accorded with the Emperor's intent; he was promoted to transport assistant of Lizhou circuit, and again served as assistant director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 為監察御史裏行，建言：「成天下之務，莫急於人才，願令兩制近臣及轉運使各得舉士。」

translations.literal: As investigating censor he memorialized, "Nothing is more urgent for accomplishing the empire's tasks than talent; I ask that Academicians of the two inner halls and circuit transport commissioners each be allowed to recommend scholars."
translations.idiomatic: As investigating censor he memorialized, "Nothing is more urgent for accomplishing the empire's tasks than talent; I ask that Academicians of the two inner halls and circuit transport commissioners each be allowed to recommend scholars."

sentences.zh: 詔各薦一人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered each to recommend one person.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered each to recommend one person.

sentences.zh: 繼言：「寒遠下僚，既得名聞於上，願令中書審其能而表用，則急才之詔，不虛行於天下矣。」

translations.literal: He memorialized further, "Junior officials far below, once their names reach the throne, I ask that the Secretariat examine their ability and memorialize appointment—then the urgent call for talent will not be vainly issued under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized further, "Junior officials far below, once their names reach the throne, I ask that the Secretariat examine their ability and memorialize appointment—then the urgent call for talent will not be issued in vain throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 又言：「比年水旱，民蒙支貸倚閣之恩，今幸歲豐，有司悉當舉催。

translations.literal: He also said, "In recent years of flood and drought the people have enjoyed the grace of relief loans and deferred collection; now that the harvest is abundant, the authorities everywhere are pressing collection in full.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In recent years of flood and drought the people have enjoyed the grace of relief loans and deferred collection; now that the harvest is abundant, the authorities everywhere are pressing collection in full.

sentences.zh: 久饑初稔，累給並償，是使民遇豐年而思歉歲也，請令諸道以漸督取之。」

translations.literal: After long famine the first good harvest, with accumulated disbursements all repaid at once—this makes the people greet a bountiful year while longing for lean years; I ask that the circuits be ordered to collect gradually."
translations.idiomatic: After long famine the first good harvest, with accumulated disbursements all repaid at once—this makes the people greet a bountiful year while longing for lean years; I ask that the circuits be ordered to collect gradually."

sentences.zh: 論俞充結王中正致宰屬，並言中正任使太重。

translations.literal: He criticized Yu Chong for associating with the eunuch Wang Zhongzheng to reach the chief minister's staff, and jointly argued that Zhongzheng's commission was too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: He criticized Yu Chong for associating with the eunuch Wang Zhongzheng to reach the chief minister's staff, and jointly argued that Zhongzheng's commission was too heavy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「人才蓋無類，顧駕御之何如耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Talent knows no category; it depends only on how one reins it in."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Talent knows no category; it depends only on how one reins it in."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「雖然，臣慮漸不可長也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Even so, Your servant fears that what grows gradually cannot be stopped in time."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Even so, Your servant fears that what grows gradually cannot be stopped in time."

sentences.zh: 河決曹村，壞田三十萬頃、民廬舍三十八萬家。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst at Caocun, ruining three hundred thousand qing of fields and thirty-eight myriad dwellings of the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River burst at Caocun, ruining three hundred thousand qing of fields and thirty-eight myriad dwellings of the people.

sentences.zh: 受詔安撫京東，發廩振饑，遠不能至者，分遣吏移給，擇高地作舍以居民，流民過所毋征算，轉行者賦糧，質私牛而與之錢，養男女棄於道者，丁壯則役其力，凡所活二十五萬。

translations.literal: Ordered to pacify the eastern capital region, he opened granaries to relieve famine; for those far beyond reach he dispatched clerks to deliver relief, chose high ground to build shelters for the displaced, exempted transit levies on roaming refugees, supplied grain to those still moving, pawned private oxen and gave money in exchange, nursed abandoned children on the roads, and conscripted strong men for labor—altogether saving two hundred fifty thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to pacify the eastern capital region, he opened granaries to relieve famine; for those far beyond reach he dispatched clerks to deliver relief, chose high ground to build shelters for the displaced, exempted transit levies on roaming refugees, supplied grain to those still on the move, pawned private oxen and gave money in exchange, nursed abandoned children on the roads, and conscripted strong men for labor—altogether saving two hundred fifty thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 相州獄起，鄧溫伯、上官均論其冤，得譴去，詔廉詰之，竟不能正。

translations.literal: When a case arose in the Xiangzhou prison, Deng Wenbo and Shangguan Jun argued the prisoners' innocence and were dismissed in reprimand; the Emperor ordered Lian to investigate, and in the end he could not rectify the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When a case arose in the Xiangzhou prison, Deng Wenbo and Shangguan Jun argued the prisoners' innocence and were dismissed in reprimand; the Emperor ordered Lian to investigate, and in the end he could not rectify the matter.

sentences.zh: 未幾獄成，始悔之。

translations.literal: Before long the case was concluded and the Emperor came to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the case was concluded and the Emperor came to regret it.

sentences.zh: 加集質校理，提點河東刑獄。

translations.literal: He was given the additional office of Collator in the Court for Collection of Precious Objects and made judicial intendant of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional office of Collator in the Court for Collection of Precious Objects and made judicial intendant of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遼人求代北地，廉言：「分水畫境，失中國險固，啟豺狼心。」

translations.literal: The Khitan sought the northern lands beyond Dai; Lian said, "Dividing the border by watercourses forfeits China's strategic strongpoints and whets the appetite of wolves."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sought the northern lands beyond Dai; Lian said, "Dividing the border by watercourses forfeits China's strategic strongpoints and whets the appetite of wolves."

sentences.zh: 其後契丹果包取兩不耕地，下臨雁門，父老以為恨。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Khitan indeed absorbed the two stretches of unsettled land, overlooking Yanmen Pass, and the elders of the region bore this as a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Khitan indeed absorbed the two stretches of unsettled land, overlooking Yanmen Pass, and the elders of the region bore this as a grievance.

sentences.zh: 王中正發西兵，用一而調二，轉運使又附益之，廉曰：「民朘剝至骨，斟酌不乏興，足矣！

translations.literal: Wang Zhongzheng mobilized western troops, requisitioning double while mustering one; the transport commissioner added still more; Lian said, "The people are stripped to the bone—careful provision is enough for the campaign without shortage!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongzheng mobilized western troops, requisitioning double while mustering one; the transport commissioner added still more; Lian said, "The people are stripped to the bone—careful provision is enough for the campaign without shortage!

sentences.zh: 忍自竭根本邪？」

translations.literal: Can you bear to exhaust the very root itself?"
translations.idiomatic: Can you bear to exhaust the very root itself?"

sentences.zh: 即奏云：「師必無功，盍有以善其後？」

translations.literal: He memorialized at once, "The army is sure to fail without success; ought there not be some means to mend matters afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized at once, "The army is sure to fail without success; ought there not be some means to mend matters afterward?"

sentences.zh: 既大軍潰歸，中正嫁罪於轉餉。

translations.literal: When the great army returned in rout, Zhongzheng shifted blame onto those who supplied provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army returned in rout, Zhongzheng shifted blame onto those who supplied provisions.

sentences.zh: 廉詣上黨對理，坐貶秩。

translations.literal: Lian went to Shangdang to argue the case in person and was demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lian went to Shangdang to argue the case in person and was demoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，進為左司郎中，遷起居郎、集賢殿修撰、樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Left Division Director; he was transferred to Diarist, Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Writings, and Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner's Court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Left Division Director, then transferred to Diarist, Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Writings, and Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner's Court.

sentences.zh: 上官均論其往附蔡確為獄，改陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: Shangguan Jun argued that in the past he had attached himself to Cai Que in the prison case; he was reassigned as Commissioner of the Shaanxi Transport Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Jun charged that he had formerly sided with Cai Que in the prison affair; he was reassigned as Commissioner of the Shaanxi Transport Circuit.

sentences.zh: 拜給事中，卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Censor-in-Chief; he died at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervising Censor-in-Chief, then died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 朱服，字行中，湖州烏程人。

translations.literal: Zhu Fu, courtesy name Xingzhong, was a native of Wucheng in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu, courtesy name Xingzhong, was a native of Wucheng in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 熙寧進士甲科，以淮南節度推官充修撰、經義局檢討，歷國子直講、秘閣校理。

translations.literal: In the Xining era he passed the jinshi examination in the first class; as judicial assistant of the Huainan circuit he served as compiler and reviewer at the Classics Meaning Bureau; he held the posts of Lecturer-at-Large in the Directorate of Education and Collator at the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xining era he graduated jinshi in the first class. As judicial assistant on the Huainan circuit he served as compiler and reviewer at the Classics Meaning Bureau, and later as Lecturer-at-Large in the Directorate of Education and Collator at the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，擢監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: During the Yuanfeng era he was elevated to Probationary Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng era he was elevated to Probationary Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 參知政事章惇遣所善袁默、周之道見服，道薦引意以市恩，服舉劾之。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councilor Zhang Dun sent his favorites Yuan Mo and Zhou Zhidao to see Fu, hinting at recommendation to curry favor; Fu impeached them.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councilor Zhang Dun sent his protégés Yuan Mo and Zhou Zhidao to visit Fu, intimating that recommendation might win his gratitude; Fu impeached them.

sentences.zh: 惇補郡，免默、之道官。

translations.literal: Dun was assigned to a prefecture; Mo and Zhidao were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was sent out to fill a prefectural post, and Mo and Zhidao were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 受詔治朱明之獄。

translations.literal: He received orders to investigate the Zhu Ming case.
translations.idiomatic: He received orders to investigate the Zhu Ming case.

sentences.zh: 故事，制獄許上殿，非本章所云者皆取旨。

translations.literal: By precedent, commissioners for special cases were permitted to attend court; on matters not covered in the original memorial they were to seek instructions.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, commissioners appointed to special cases were allowed to appear at court; on any matter not covered in the original memorial they had to seek the throne's instruction.

sentences.zh: 服論其非是，罷之。

translations.literal: Fu argued this was wrong, and the practice was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Fu argued that this was wrong, and the practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 俄知諫院，遷國子司業、起居舍人，以直龍圖閣知潤州，徙泉、婺、寧、廬、壽五州。

translations.literal: Soon he was put in charge of the Remonstrance Bureau; promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and Diarist-of-the-Left; with the honorary title of Associate at the Dragon Diagram Hall he was prefect of Runzhou, then transferred successively to Quan, Wu, Ning, Lu, and Shou prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was placed in charge of the Remonstrance Bureau, then promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and Diarist-of-the-Left. With the honorary title Associate at the Dragon Diagram Hall he governed Runzhou, and was later transferred in turn through Quan, Wu, Ning, Lu, and Shou.

sentences.zh: 廬人饑，守便宜振護，全活十餘萬口。

translations.literal: When the people of Luzhou were starving, as prefect he used discretionary authority to relieve and protect them, saving more than a hundred thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Luzhou were starving, he used his authority as prefect to relieve and protect them at need, saving more than a hundred thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 明年大疫，又課醫持善藥分拯之，賴以安省甚眾。

translations.literal: The next year when a great pestilence struck, he also assigned physicians with good medicines to distribute relief; many thus found peace.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when a great pestilence struck, he also set physicians with effective medicines to distribute aid; many were thereby restored to peace.

sentences.zh: 當元祐時，未嘗一日在朝廷，不能無少望。

translations.literal: During the Yuanyou era he was never a single day at court, and could not be without some disappointment.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Yuanyou era he never spent a single day at court, and could not altogether suppress a measure of disappointment.

sentences.zh: 值紹聖初政，因表賀，乃力詆變亂法度之故。

translations.literal: When the opening policies of Shaosheng came, on submitting a congratulatory memorial he forcefully denounced the reasons for overturning and disrupting the legal order.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shaosheng reign he submitted a congratulatory memorial and thereupon denounced with force the reasons the legal order had been overturned and thrown into confusion.

sentences.zh: 召為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Drafting Official of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Drafting Official of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 使遼，未反而母死，詔以其家貧，賜帛二百。

translations.literal: On an embassy to Liao, before he returned his mother died; an edict said because his household was poor, two hundred bolts of silk were granted.
translations.idiomatic: While on embassy to Liao, before he could return his mother died; an edict, noting that his household was poor, granted him two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 喪除，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 湖州守馬城言其居喪疏几筵而獨處它室，謫知萊州。

translations.literal: Prefect Ma Cheng of Huzhou said that during mourning he kept the mourning couch sparse while living alone in another room; he was demoted to prefect of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Huzhou, Ma Cheng, reported that during mourning he had kept only a sparse couch for the bier yet lived alone in another room; he was demoted to prefect of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，加集賢殿修撰，再為廬州；

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended, he was given the additional title Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Writings and again served at Luzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, he was given the additional title of Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Writings and again governed Luzhou;

sentences.zh: 越兩月，徙廣州。

translations.literal: Within two months he was transferred to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later he was transferred to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 哲宗既祥，服賦詩有「孤臣正泣龍髯草」之語，為部使者所上，黜知袁州。

translations.literal: After Emperor Zhezong's xiang mourning ended, Fu composed a poem with the line "this lonely minister weeps before the dragon's beard grass"; it was reported by a circuit commissioner; he was removed to prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhezong's second-year mourning had ended, Fu wrote a poem containing the line "a lone minister weeps before the dragon's-beard grass"; a circuit commissioner reported it, and he was removed to govern Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又坐與蘇軾遊，貶海州團練副使，蘄州安置。

translations.literal: Again for associating with Su Shi he was demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Haizhou, with residence ordered at Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Again, for associating with Su Shi, he was demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Haizhou and ordered to reside at Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 改興國軍，卒。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to Xingguo Army; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Xingguo Army, where he died.

sentences.zh: 張舜民

translations.literal: Zhang Shunmin
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shunmin

sentences.zh: 張舜民，字芸叟，邠州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shunmin, courtesy name Yunsou, was a native of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shunmin, courtesy name Yunsou, was a native of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，為襄樂令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was magistrate of Xiangle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and became magistrate of Xiangle.

sentences.zh: 王安石倡新法，舜民上書言：「便民所以窮民，強內所以弱內，辟國所以蹙國。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi advocated the New Policies; Shunmin submitted a memorial saying: "What is meant to benefit the people in fact impoverishes them; what is meant to strengthen the interior in fact weakens it; what is meant to open the realm in fact contracts it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi championed the New Policies. Shunmin submitted a memorial saying, "Measures meant to ease life for the people in fact impoverish them; measures meant to strengthen the interior in fact weaken it; measures meant to expand the realm in fact shrink it.

sentences.zh: 以堂堂之天下，而與小民爭利， 可恥也。」

translations.literal: For the resplendent empire to compete with common people for profit—is shameful."
translations.idiomatic: For a realm as grand as ours to wrangle with common folk over profit—how shameful."

sentences.zh: 時人壯之。

translations.literal: People of the time admired him for it.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，朝廷討西夏，陳留縣五路出兵，環慶帥高遵裕辟掌機密文字。

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng the court campaigned against Western Xia; armies were dispatched from five routes through Chenliu; Commander Gao Zunyu of the Huanqing circuit recruited him to manage confidential documents.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng era the court campaigned against Western Xia. Five armies marched out through Chenliu; Gao Zunyu, commander of the Huanqing circuit, recruited Shunmin to manage confidential documents.

sentences.zh: 王師無功，舜民在靈武詩有「白骨似沙沙似雪」，及官軍「斫受降城柳為薪」之句，坐謫監邕州鹽米倉；

translations.literal: The imperial armies achieved nothing; at Lingwu Shunmin wrote in verse "white bones like sand, sand like snow" and of the troops "felling willows at Shouxiang City for firewood"; for this he was demoted to overseer of the Yongzhou salt-and-grain depot;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armies won nothing. At Lingwu Shunmin wrote in verse, "White bones like sand, sand like snow," and of the troops, "They hew the willows of Shouxiang City for firewood." For this he was demoted to overseer of the Yongzhou salt-and-grain depot;

sentences.zh: 又追赴鄜延詔獄，改監郴州酒稅。

translations.literal: Again he was summoned to the edict prison at Fuyan, then reassigned to oversee wine taxes at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then summoned to the edict prison at Fuyan and afterward reassigned to oversee wine taxes at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 會赦北還，司馬光薦其才氣秀異，剛直敢言，以館閣校勘為監察御史。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came he returned north; Sima Guang recommended his outstanding talent and spirit, his forthright courage in speech; from collation in the palace libraries he became Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty was proclaimed he returned north. Sima Guang recommended his exceptional talent and spirit and his forthright, fearless speech; from collation in the palace libraries he was made Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 上疏論西夏強臣爭權，不宜加以爵命，當興師問罪，因及文彥博，左遷監登聞鼓院。
