translations.literal: He memorialized that powerful ministers of Western Xia were struggling for power and should not be granted titles; the court ought to raise troops and demand accountability—thereby touching on Wen Yanbo; he was demoted to overseer of the Petition Drum Court.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that powerful ministers of Western Xia were contending for power and ought not to receive enfeoffment; the court should raise an army and call them to account—thereby implicating Wen Yanbo. He was demoted to overseer of the Petition Drum Court.

sentences.zh: 臺諫交章乞還職，不聽。

translations.literal: Censors and remonstrators submitted memorials in succession asking that he be restored; the court did not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and remonstrators submitted memorial after memorial asking that he be restored to office, but the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 通判虢州，提點秦鳳刑獄。

translations.literal: Vice prefect of Guozhou; intendant of judicial affairs in the Qinfeng circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of Guozhou and as intendant of judicial affairs on the Qinfeng circuit.

sentences.zh: 召拜殿中侍御史，固辭，改金部員外郎。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Palace Attendant Censor; he firmly declined and was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Palace Attendant Censor, but firmly declined; he was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue instead.

sentences.zh: 進秘書少監，使遼，加直秘閣、陝西轉運使，知陝、潭、青三州。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat; on embassy to Liao; given direct access to the Secret Archive and made Shaanxi transport commissioner; prefect of Shaan, Tan, and Qing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, served on embassy to Liao, was given direct access to the Secret Archive, and became Shaanxi transport commissioner, governing in turn Shaan, Tan, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 元符中，罷職付東銓，以為坊州、鳳翔，皆不赴。

translations.literal: During Yuanfu his office was terminated and he was handed to the eastern selection board; he was appointed to Fangzhou and Fengxiang but went to neither.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era his office was terminated and he was handed over to the eastern selection board. He was appointed to Fangzhou and Fengxiang but went to neither post.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，擢右諫議大夫，居職才七日，所上事已六十章。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended he was elevated to Right Remonstrance Advisor; he had been in office only seven days when his submitted matters already numbered sixty memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended the throne he was elevated to Right Remonstrance Advisor. He had been in office only seven days when the matters he had submitted already numbered sixty memorials.

sentences.zh: 陳陝西之弊曰：「以庸將而御老師，役饑民而爭曠土。」

translations.literal: He laid out the ills of Shaanxi, saying: "Mediocre generals are set over veteran armies; starving people are forced to labor for contested wasteland."
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the ills of Shaanxi, saying, "Mediocre generals are set over veteran armies; starving people are driven to fight over barren land."

sentences.zh: 極論河朔之困，言多剴峭。

translations.literal: He argued exhaustively the distress of Hebei; his words were mostly sharp and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: He argued at length the distress of Hebei; his language was mostly sharp and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 徙吏部侍郎，旋以龍圖閣待制知定州，改同州。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel; soon made Dragon Diagram Hall academician-administrator and prefect of Dingzhou; transferred to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, then soon made academician-administrator of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Dingzhou, and later transferred to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐元祐黨，謫楚州團練副使，商州安置。

translations.literal: For association with the Yuanyou faction he was demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Chuzhou, residence ordered at Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For association with the Yuanyou faction he was demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Chuzhou and ordered to reside at Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 復集賢殿修撰，卒。

translations.literal: Restored as Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Writings; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Writings, then died.

sentences.zh: 舜民慷慨喜論事，善為文，自號「浮休居士」。

translations.literal: Shunmin was magnanimous and loved to debate affairs; skilled at writing; he styled himself "Hermit of Floating Rest."
translations.idiomatic: Shunmin was open-handed and loved to debate public affairs; he was skilled at writing and styled himself the Hermit of Floating Rest.

sentences.zh: 其使遼也，見其太孫禧好音樂、美姝、名茶、古畫，以為他日必有如唐張義潮挈十三州來歸者，不四十年當見之。

translations.literal: On his embassy to Liao he saw the great-grandson Xi fond of music, beautiful women, fine tea, and antique paintings; he thought that someday there would surely be someone like Tang's Zhang Yichao who would lead the thirteen circuits back in submission—within forty years one would see it.
translations.idiomatic: On his embassy to Liao he observed the great-grandson Xi to be fond of music, beautiful women, fine tea, and antique paintings. He concluded that one day there would surely appear another Zhang Yichao of Tang, who would lead the thirteen circuits back in submission—and that within forty years one would see it.

sentences.zh: 後如其言。

translations.literal: Later it came to pass as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Later events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，追贈寶文閣直學士。

translations.literal: During Shaoxing he was posthumously granted Academic Gentlemen of the Hall for Treasuring Culture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing era he was posthumously granted the title Academic Gentlemen of the Hall for Treasuring Culture.

sentences.zh: 盛陶，字仲叔，鄭州人。

translations.literal: Sheng Tao, courtesy name Zhongshu, was a native of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Tao, courtesy name Zhongshu, was a native of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，為監察御史。

translations.literal: During Xining he was Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era he served as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 神宗問河北事，對曰：「朝廷以便民省役，議廢郡縣，誠便。

translations.literal: Shenzong asked about Hebei affairs; he replied: "The court, to benefit the people and reduce corvée, discusses abolishing prefectures and counties—truly convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong asked about affairs in Hebei, he replied, "The court, wishing to benefit the people and reduce corvée, is discussing the abolition of prefectures and counties—which would indeed be convenient.

sentences.zh: 然沿邊地相屬，如北平至海不過五百里，其間列城十五，祖宗之意固有所在，願仍舊貫。」

translations.literal: Yet along the border the territory is continuous; from Beiping to the sea is not five hundred li; within it are fifteen walled cities—the intent of the ancestors surely has its reason; I hope the old system may be kept."
translations.idiomatic: Yet along the frontier the land runs continuously: from Beiping to the sea is scarcely five hundred li, and within that stretch stand fifteen walled cities. The intent of the ancestors surely had its reason; I beg that the old arrangement be preserved."

sentences.zh: 慶州李復圭輕敵敗國，程昉開河無功，籍水政以擾州縣，皆疏其過。

translations.literal: Li Fugui of Qingzhou was contemptuous of the enemy and brought defeat on the state; Cheng Fang opened a canal without success; registering water administration to harass prefectures and counties—all his wrongdoing he memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fugui of Qingzhou treated the enemy lightly and brought defeat on the state; Cheng Fang opened a canal without success and used water administration to harass prefectures and counties—Tao memorialized the faults of them all.

sentences.zh: 二人實王安石所主，陶不少屈，出簽書隨州判官。

translations.literal: Both men were in fact Wang Anshi's protégés; Tao would not yield in the least and was sent out as signing clerk and judge of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were in fact protégés of Wang Anshi. Tao would not yield in the least and was sent out as signing clerk and judge of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，入為太常博士、考功員外郎、工部右司郎中，至侍御史。

translations.literal: After a long while he entered as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Right Division Director in the Ministry of Works, reaching Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he entered court service as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Right Division Director in the Ministry of Works, eventually reaching Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 陳官冗之敝，謂恩澤舉人，宜取嘉祐、治平之制；

translations.literal: He laid out the ill of redundant offices, saying candidates by grace and favor should follow the Jiaoyou and Zhiping system;
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the ill of redundant offices, saying that candidates advanced by grace and favor ought to follow the Jiaoyou and Zhiping system;

sentences.zh: 選人改官，宜準熙寧、元豐之法。

translations.literal: selected men changing office should follow the Xining and Yuanfeng law.
translations.idiomatic: and that selected men changing office ought to follow the Xining and Yuanfeng law.

sentences.zh: 諫官劉安世等攻蔡確為謗詩，陶曰：「確以弟碩有罪，但坐罷職，不應懷恨。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Liu Anshi and others attacked Cai Que for slanderous poetry; Tao said: "Que's younger brother Shuo had guilt; he was only dismissed from office—he ought not to harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When remonstrance officials Liu Anshi and others attacked Cai Que for slanderous poetry, Tao said, "Que's younger brother Shuo was guilty, yet Que was only dismissed from office—he ought not to harbor resentment.

sentences.zh: 注釋詩語，近於捃摭，不可以長告訐之風。」

translations.literal: Annotating poetic phrases comes close to nitpicking; one cannot allow the fashion of lengthy informing to grow."
translations.idiomatic: To annotate lines of poetry comes close to nitpicking; one cannot allow the fashion of lengthy informing to grow."

sentences.zh: 安世疏言：「陶居風憲地，目睹無禮於君親之人，而附會觀望，紀綱何賴。」

translations.literal: Anshi memorialized: "Tao holds a post of censorial wind; he witnessed men disrespectful to lord and parent yet temporized and looked on—on what can discipline rely?"
translations.idiomatic: Anshi memorialized, "Tao holds a post charged with upholding censorial discipline. He has witnessed men disrespectful toward lord and parent, yet he temporizes and looks on—on what, then, can public order rely?"

sentences.zh: 出知汝州，徙晉州，召為太常少卿。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Ruzhou; transferred to Jinzhou; summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Ruzhou, transferred to Jinzhou, and later summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 議合祭天地，請從先帝北郊之旨；

translations.literal: Discussing combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, he asked to follow the late emperor's intent for the northern suburban sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, he asked that it follow the late emperor's intent for the northern suburban sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 既而合祭，陶即奉行，亦不復辨執也。

translations.literal: when combined sacrifice was adopted, Tao simply carried it out and did not argue further either.
translations.idiomatic: but once combined sacrifice was adopted, Tao simply carried it out and did not press his earlier view.

sentences.zh: 進權禮部侍郎、中書舍人，以龍圖閣待制知應天府、順昌府、瀛州。

translations.literal: Promoted to Acting Vice Minister of Rites and Drafting Official of the Central Secretariat; as Dragon Diagram academician-administrator he was prefect of Yingtian, Shunchang, and Ying prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Vice Minister of Rites and Drafting Official of the Central Secretariat, and as academician-administrator of the Dragon Diagram Hall governed Yingtian, Shunchang, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 元符中，例奪職，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: During Yuanfu, by precedent his office was stripped; he died at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era his office was stripped by precedent; he died at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王氏、章、蔡之當國也，士大夫知拂之必斥，附之必進也，而孫鼛正言蔡京，不肯為之助；

translations.literal: The comment says: When the Wang clan, Zhang, and Cai held power, scholar-officials knew that to oppose them was surely to be expelled and to join them was surely to advance; yet Sun Gao spoke plainly against Cai Jing and would not assist him;
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: When the Wang clan, Zhang Dun, and Cai Que held the state, scholar-officials knew that to oppose them was to be expelled and to join them was to advance. Yet Sun Gao spoke plainly against Cai Jing and would not lend him aid;

sentences.zh: 吳時卻童貫，忤王黼，乃幸於罷歸；

translations.literal: Wu Shi rebuffed Tong Guan and offended Wang Fu, yet was fortunate to be dismissed and return home;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shi rebuffed Tong Guan and offended Wang Fu, yet was fortunate enough to be dismissed and return home;

sentences.zh: 昭玘辭侯蒙之延致；

translations.literal: Li Zhaoqi declined Hou Meng's invitation;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhaoqi declined Hou Meng's invitation to serve;

sentences.zh: 朱服發章惇之薦引，舜民詆新法；

translations.literal: Zhu Fu exposed Zhang Dun's recommendation; Shunmin denounced the New Policies;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu exposed Zhang Dun's attempt at recommendation; Shunmin denounced the New Policies;

sentences.zh: 而盛陶不屈於安石，其大節皆可取。

translations.literal: and Sheng Tao would not yield to Anshi—all their great integrity is admirable.
translations.idiomatic: and Sheng Tao would not yield to Anshi—in all these cases their great integrity is worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 獨漢之為京客，黃廉附蔡確獄，有愧鼛等多矣。

translations.literal: Only Wang Hanzhi as Jing's client and Huang Lian joining Cai Que's prison case—how much more ashamed than Sun Gao and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Hanzhi, as a client of Cai Jing, and Huang Lian, who joined Cai Que's prison case, stand far more ashamed than Sun Gao and the others.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「介於石，不終日，貞吉。」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Between the stone, not a whole day—perseverance brings good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Caught between the stones—before the day is out. Perseverance brings good fortune."

sentences.zh: 故君子貴乎知幾。

translations.literal: Thus the gentleman values knowing the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the gentleman prizes knowing the turning point in time.

sentences.zh: 章衡，字子平，浦城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng, courtesy name Ziping, was a native of Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng, courtesy name Ziping, was a native of Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，進士第一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou he came in first in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiayou he placed first in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 通判湖州，直集賢院，改鹽鐵判官，同修起居注。

translations.literal: Vice prefect of Huzhou, direct appointment at the Hall for Collecting Writings, transferred to Salt and Iron Commissioner, jointly edited the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of Huzhou, received direct appointment at the Hall for Collecting Writings, was transferred to Salt and Iron Commissioner, and jointly edited the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 物有掛空籍者，奏請蠲之。

translations.literal: Items hanging on empty registers—he memorialized to have them exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Where items hung on empty registers, he memorialized to have the obligations remitted.

sentences.zh: 又言：「三司經費，取領而無多寡，率不預知。

translations.literal: He also said: "The three departments' expenditures—funds are drawn without knowing amounts; as a rule they are not foreknown in advance.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In the expenditures of the three departments, funds are drawn without knowing the amounts; as a rule no one foreknows them in advance.

sentences.zh: 急則斂於民，倉卒趣迫，故苦其難供。

translations.literal: In urgency they are levied on the people; in haste and pressure, hence the hardship of supply.
translations.idiomatic: When urgency comes, levies fall on the people; pressed in haste, they suffer under the burden of supply.

sentences.zh: 願敕三部判官，簿正其數，即有所賦，先期下之，使公私皆濟。」

translations.literal: I wish that the three departments' vice commissioners be ordered to register and correct the figures; when there is something to be assigned, issue it in advance, so that public and private may both be aided."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the vice commissioners of the three departments be ordered to register and correct the figures, and that whenever an assessment is due it be issued in advance, so that both public and private interests may be served."

sentences.zh: 三司使忌其能，出知汝州、 潁州。

translations.literal: The three departments commissioner resented his ability; he was sent out as prefect of Ruzhou and Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner of the three departments resented his ability and had him sent out as prefect of Ruzhou and Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，還判太常寺。

translations.literal: At the start of Xining he returned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era he returned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 建言：「自唐開元纂修禮書，以《國恤》一章為豫凶事，刪而去之。

translations.literal: He proposed: "From the Tang Kaiyuan compilation of ritual books, taking the chapter 'National Mourning' as foreknowledge of misfortune, it was cut and removed.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed, "When the Tang, in the Kaiyuan reign, compiled ritual books, they treated the chapter 'National Mourning' as foreknowledge of misfortune and cut it away.

sentences.zh: 故不幸遇事，則捃摭墜殘，茫無所據。

translations.literal: Hence when misfortune occurs unexpectedly, one gropes through fallen fragments with nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Hence when misfortune strikes unexpectedly, officials grope among fallen fragments with nothing solid to rely on.

sentences.zh: 今宜為《厚陵集禮》，以貽萬世。」

translations.literal: Now one ought to compile 'Collected Rites of the Thick Tumulus' to hand down to ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Now the court ought to compile a Collected Rites of the Thick Tumulus to hand down to ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 出知鄭州，奏罷原武監，馳牧地四千二百頃以予民。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou; memorialized to abolish the Yuanyuan monitor, racing four thousand two hundred qing of pasture land to grant the people.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou, he memorialized to abolish the Yuanyuan monitor and rushed four thousand two hundred qing of pasture land into the people's hands.

sentences.zh: 復判太常，知審官西院。

translations.literal: Again vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; knew the Western Office of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and as director of the Western Office of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 使遼，燕射連發破的，遼以為文武兼備，待之異於他使。

translations.literal: On embassy to Liao, at the banquet archery he hit the mark repeatedly; Liao considered him endowed with both civil and military talent and treated him differently from other envoys.
translations.idiomatic: On embassy to Liao, at the banquet archery he hit the mark again and again. The Liao court judged him to combine civil and military gifts and treated him differently from other envoys.

sentences.zh: 歸復命，言遼境無備，因此時可復山後八州。

translations.literal: On return he reported that the Liao border was undefended and that at this time the eight prefectures behind the mountains could be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported that the Liao frontier was undefended and that at this moment the eight prefectures behind the mountains could be recovered.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The court did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 衡患學者不知古今，纂歷代帝系，名曰《編年通載》，神宗覽而善之，謂可冠冕諸史；

translations.literal: Heng worried that scholars did not know past and present; he compiled successive imperial lines, titled Comprehensive Chronological Record; Shenzong read it with approval and said it could crown all histories;
translations.idiomatic: Heng worried that scholars did not know past from present. He compiled successive imperial lines in a work titled Comprehensive Chronological Record. Shenzong read it with approval and said it could crown all histories;

sentences.zh: 且念其嘗先多士，進用獨後，面賜三品服。

translations.literal: and reflecting that he had once led the talented but was promoted later than many, face to face he granted third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: and reflecting that though he had once led the foremost scholars, his own advancement had come late, he granted him third-rank robes in person.

sentences.zh: 判吏部流內銓，嘗有員闕，既擬注，而三班院輒用之，反訟吏部。

translations.literal: As vice director of the Ministry of Personnel's flowing-within board: there was once a vacancy; after nominations were drawn up the Three-Rank Court used it instead and sued the Ministry of Personnel in turn.
translations.idiomatic: As vice director of the Ministry of Personnel's flowing-within selection board, there was once a vacancy. After nominations had been drawn up, the Three-Rank Court used the post instead and in turn brought suit against the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宰相主其說，衡連奏疏與之辨。

translations.literal: The chief councilor supported their claim; Heng submitted memorials in succession disputing with them.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor supported their claim. Heng submitted memorial after memorial disputing them.

sentences.zh: 或曰宰相之勢，恐不可深校，衡不為止，至訴於御前。

translations.literal: Someone said the chief councilor's power—one fears it cannot be deeply challenged; Heng did not stop, even appealing before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said the chief councilor's power was such that one ought not press the matter too far; Heng would not stop, and carried the dispute before the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 神宗命內侍偕至中書，宰相見之怒，衡曰：「衡為朝廷法耳。」

translations.literal: Shenzong ordered an inner attendant to accompany him to the Central Secretariat; the chief councilor saw this and was angry; Heng said: "Heng upholds the law for the court."
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong ordered an inner attendant to accompany Heng to the Central Secretariat. When the chief councilor saw this he was angry. Heng said, "Heng upholds the law on behalf of the court."

sentences.zh: 以狀上請而視之，相悟曰：「若爾，吏部是矣。」

translations.literal: He submitted a written plea and asked him to read it; the councilor understood and said: "If so, the Ministry of Personnel is right."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a written statement and asked the councilor to read it. The councilor understood and said, "If that is so, the Ministry of Personnel is in the right."

sentences.zh: 乃罪三班。

translations.literal: So the Three-Rank Court was punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Three-Rank Court was thereupon punished.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知通進銀臺司、直舍人院，拜寶文閣待制、知澶州。

translations.literal: Before long he was put in charge of the Communication and Silver Terrace Office and the Drafting Courtyard; appointed Academic Administrator of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and prefect of Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was placed in charge of the Communication and Silver Terrace Office and the Drafting Courtyard, and was appointed academician-administrator of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and prefect of Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「卿為仁宗朝魁甲，寶文藏御集之處，未始除人，今以之處卿。」

translations.literal: Shenzong said: "You were top graduate in Renzong's reign; the Hall for Treasuring Culture stores the imperial collections—never before had a man been appointed there; now it is given to you."
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong said, "You were top graduate in Renzong's reign. The Hall for Treasuring Culture houses the imperial collections—never before had anyone been appointed there. Now that honor is given to you."

sentences.zh: 衡拜謝。

translations.literal: Heng bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Heng bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 至郡，會官立法禁民販鹽，衡言：「民恃鹽以生，生之所在，雖犯法不顧。

translations.literal: On reaching the prefecture, officials were legislating to forbid the people from trafficking salt; Heng said: "The people depend on salt to live; where livelihood lies, though it violates law they do not care.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his prefecture, officials were drafting a law forbidding the people to traffic in salt. Heng said, "The people depend on salt to live. Where livelihood is at stake, they will break the law without a second thought.

sentences.zh: 空令犴獄日繁，請如故便。」

translations.literal: Emptyly making prisons fill day by day—please allow matters as before for convenience."
translations.idiomatic: We would only fill the prisons day by day for nothing. I ask that matters be left as before for the people's convenience."

sentences.zh: 徙知成德軍，坐事免。

translations.literal: Transferred to prefect of Chengde Army; dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Chengde Army, then dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，歷秀、襄、河陽、曹、蘇州，加集賢院學士，復以待制知揚、廬、宣、潁州，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou he held Xiuzhou, Xiangzhou, Heyang, Cao, and Suzhou; added Academic Gentlemen of the Collecting Writings Hall; again as academician-administrator was prefect of Yang, Lu, Xuan, and Ying prefectures; he died at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era he governed in turn Xiuzhou, Xiangzhou, Heyang, Cao, and Suzhou, was made Academic Gentlemen of the Collecting Writings Hall, and again served as academician-administrator at Yang, Lu, Xuan, and Ying; he died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 顏復，字長道，魯人，顏子四十八世孫也。

translations.literal: Yan Fu, courtesy name Changdao, a man of Lu—forty-eighth-generation descendant of Yan Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Fu, courtesy name Changdao, was a man of Lu and the forty-eighth-generation descendant of Yan Hui.

sentences.zh: 父太初，以名儒為國子監直講，出為臨晉簿。

translations.literal: His father Taichu, a renowned scholar, was Lecturer-at-Large in the Directorate of Education; sent out as clerk of Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Taichu, a renowned scholar, served as Lecturer-at-Large in the Directorate of Education and was later sent out as clerk of Linjin.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，詔郡國敦訪遺逸，京東以復言。

translations.literal: In Jiayou an edict ordered circuits and prefectures to seek out reclusive talent; the Jingdong circuit recommended Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiayou era an edict ordered circuits and prefectures to seek out reclusive talent; the Jingdong circuit recommended Fu.

sentences.zh: 凡試於中書者二十有二人，考官歐陽修奏復第一。

translations.literal: All who were examined at the Central Secretariat numbered twenty-two; examining official Ouyang Xiu memorialized Fu first.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two candidates were examined at the Central Secretariat; the examining official Ouyang Xiu memorialized that Fu should rank first.

sentences.zh: 賜進士，為校書郎，知永寧縣。

translations.literal: Granted jinshi; Proofreader; magistrate of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the jinshi degree, appointed Proofreader, and made magistrate of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，為國子直講。

translations.literal: During Xining, Lecturer-at-Large in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era he served as Lecturer-at-Large in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 王安石更學法，取士率以己意，使常秩等校諸直講所出題及所考卷，定其優劣，復等五人皆罷。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi revised the learning law; selection of scholars followed his intent; he had Chang Zhi and others collate topics set by the lecturers-at-large and examination papers, fixing superior and inferior—Fu and five others were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi revised the learning law and chose scholars according to his own judgment. He had Chang Zhi and others collate the examination topics set by the lecturers-at-large and the papers submitted, fixing superior and inferior ranks—Fu and five others were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，召為太常博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou summoned as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was summoned as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 建言：「士民禮制不立，下無矜式。

translations.literal: He proposed: "Ritual for scholars and commoners is not established; below there is no model to take pride in.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed, "Ritual for scholars and commoners has not been established; below the throne there is no model for others to take pride in.

sentences.zh: 請令禮官會萃古今典範為五禮書。

translations.literal: Please order ritual officials to assemble ancient and modern paradigms into a book of the five rituals.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that ritual officials assemble ancient and modern paradigms into a book of the five rites.

sentences.zh: 又請考正祀典，凡干讖緯曲學、汙條陋製、道流醮謝、術家厭勝之法，一切芟去。

translations.literal: He also asked to examine and correct the sacrificial canon: all heterodox prognostication, vulgar regulations, Taoist offerings, and occult suppression practices—cut them all away.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to examine and correct the sacrificial canon: every heterodox use of omens and prognostication, vulgar regulation, Taoist offering, and occult rite of suppression should be cut away.

sentences.zh: 俾大小群祀盡合聖人之經，為後世法。」

translations.literal: So that great and small sacrifices may all accord with the sage's classics and be a law for later generations."
translations.idiomatic: Thus great and small sacrifices alike may accord with the sages' classics and stand as law for later generations."

sentences.zh: 遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 孔宗翰請尊奉孔子祠，復因上五議，欲專其祠饗，優其田祿，蠲其廟幹，司其法則，訓其子孫。

translations.literal: Kong Zonghan asked to honor Confucius's shrine; Fu added five proposals—wishing to concentrate its sacrifices, improve its field stipends, exempt its temple timber, supervise its rites, and instruct its descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Zonghan asked to honor Confucius's shrine, Fu added five proposals: to concentrate its sacrifices, improve its field stipends, exempt its temple timber, supervise its rites, and instruct its descendants.

sentences.zh: 朝廷多從之。

translations.literal: The court largely followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court largely followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 兼崇政殿說書，進起居舍人兼侍講，轉起居郎。

translations.literal: Concurrently lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall; promoted to Diarist-of-the-Left and concurrent lecturer; transferred to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently lectured at the Chongzheng Hall, was promoted to Diarist-of-the-Left with concurrent lecture duties, and was later transferred to Diarist.

sentences.zh: 請擇經行之儒，補諸縣教官；

translations.literal: He asked to select Confucian scholars of moral conduct to fill county instructors;
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Confucian scholars of proven moral conduct be chosen to fill county instructorships;

sentences.zh: 凡學者考其志業，不由教官薦，不得與貢舉、升太學。

translations.literal: all students' ambitions and work were examined—without instructor recommendation they could not participate in tribute selection or enter the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: and that all students' ambitions and work be examined—without an instructor's recommendation they should not be allowed to compete in tribute selection or enter the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 拜中書舍人兼國子監祭酒，言：「太學諸生，有誘進之法，獨教官未嘗旌別，似非嚴師勸士之道。」

translations.literal: Appointed Drafting Official of the Central Secretariat and concurrent Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; he said: "Directorate students have methods to encourage advancement; only instructors have never been distinguished in reward—it seems not the way of strict teachers to urge scholars."
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Drafting Official of the Central Secretariat and concurrent Chancellor of the Directorate of Education. He said, "Directorate students have methods to encourage advancement, yet instructors alone have never been singled out for reward—this hardly seems the way for strict teachers to urge their scholars."

sentences.zh: 未逾年，以疾改天章閣待制，未拜而卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: Within a year, on illness he was changed to academician-administrator of the Hall of Heavenly Pattern; before taking office he died at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year, on grounds of illness, he was reassigned as academician-administrator of the Hall of Heavenly Pattern. Before he could take up the post he died at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 王岩叟等言復學行超特，宜加優賻，詔賜錢五十萬。

translations.literal: Wang Yansou and others said Fu's learning and conduct were exceptional and he should receive added posthumous favor; an edict granted five hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yansou and others said Fu's learning and conduct were exceptional and that added posthumous honors were fitting; an edict granted five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 子岐，建炎中為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Qi, during Jianyan was Vice Censor-in-Chief under the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi, during the Jianyan era, served as Vice Censor-in-Chief under the Gate.

sentences.zh: 孫升，字君孚，高郵人。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng, courtesy name Junfu, a native of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng, courtesy name Junfu, was a native of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，簽書泰州判官。

translations.literal: Passed jinshi; signing clerk and judge of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as signing clerk and judge of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，為監察御史。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended, he became Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong ascended the throne, he became Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷更法度，逐姦邪，升多所建明。

translations.literal: The court renewed the laws and drove out the wicked; Sheng contributed many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The court renewed the laws and drove out the wicked; Sheng contributed many proposals of his own.

sentences.zh: 嘗上疏曰：「自二聖臨御，登用正人，天下所謂忠信端良之士，豪傑俊偉之材，俱收並用，近世得賢之盛，未有如今日者。

translations.literal: Once he memorialized saying: "Since the two sovereigns assumed rule, upright men have been elevated; all in the empire called loyal, trustworthy, upright, and good men, heroic and outstanding talents, were gathered and employed together—in recent times the abundance of gaining the worthy has never been like today.
translations.idiomatic: Once he memorialized, saying, "Since the two sovereigns assumed rule, upright men have been elevated. Every man in the empire accounted loyal, trustworthy, upright, and good, every heroic and outstanding talent, has been gathered and employed together. In recent times the abundance of worthy men in office has never matched today.

sentences.zh: 君子日進而小人日退，正道日長而邪慝日消，在廷濟濟有成周之風，此首開言路之效也。

translations.literal: The gentleman advances daily and the petty man retreats daily; the correct Way grows daily and wickedness daily fades; in court there is the flourishing style of prosperous Zhou—this is the effect of first opening the path of speech.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman advances day by day and the petty man retreats day by day; the correct Way lengthens day by day and wickedness wanes day by day. In court there is the flourishing style of prosperous Zhou. This is the fruit of first opening the path of free speech.

sentences.zh: 願於耳目之臣，論議之際，置黨附之疑，杜小人之隙；

translations.literal: I hope that among ears-and-eyes officials, in the midst of discussion, party attachment may be set aside and petty men's gaps sealed;
translations.idiomatic: I pray that among the officials who are the emperor's eyes and ears, in the midst of debate, suspicions of faction may be set aside and the petty man's openings sealed shut;

sentences.zh: 疑間一開，則言者不安其職矣。

translations.literal: Once suspicion opens a crack, then those who speak cannot be secure in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: for once suspicion opens even a crack, those who speak cannot rest secure in their duties.

sentences.zh: 言者不安其職，則循默之風熾，而壅蔽之患生，非朝廷之福也。」

translations.literal: When speakers cannot be secure in their duties, the fashion of following silence flourishes and the harm of obstruction arises—not a blessing to the court."
translations.idiomatic: When speakers cannot rest secure in their duties, the fashion of following silence grows fierce and the harm of obstruction arises. That is no blessing to the court."

sentences.zh: 遷殿中待御史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 梁燾責張問，升從而擊之，執政指為附和，出知濟州。

translations.literal: Liang Dao censured Zhang Wen; Sheng followed in attacking him; the chief administrators called it parroting and sent him out as prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Dao censured Zhang Wen, Sheng joined in attacking him. The chief administrators called this mere parroting and sent him out as prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，提點京西刑獄，召為金部員外郎，復拜殿中侍御史，進侍御史。

translations.literal: After a year, intendant of judicial affairs in the Jingxi circuit; summoned as Vice Director in Ministry of Revenue; again appointed Palace Attendant Censor; advanced to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he became intendant of judicial affairs on the Jingxi circuit, was summoned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was again appointed Palace Attendant Censor, and advanced to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 時翰林承旨鄧溫伯為臺臣所攻，升與賈易論之尤力，謂草蔡確制，稱其定策功比漢周勃，欺天負國，豈宜親承密命？

translations.literal: At the time Hanlin Academician Deng Wenbo was attacked by censorial officials; Sheng with Jia Yi argued most forcefully, saying he had drafted Cai Que's edict calling his settle-the-crisis merit comparable to Han's Zhou Bo—deceiving Heaven and betraying the state—how could he personally receive secret orders?
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Hanlin Academician Deng Wenbo was under attack from censorial officials. Sheng, together with Jia Yi, argued most forcefully that Wenbo had drafted Cai Que's edict, praising his merit in settling the crisis as comparable to Han's Zhou Bo—deceiving Heaven and betraying the state. How could such a man personally receive secret imperial orders?

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response.
translations.idiomatic: There was no response.

sentences.zh: 由起居郎擢中書舍人，直學士院，以天章閣待制知應天府。

translations.literal: From Diarist he was elevated to Drafting Official of the Central Secretariat and direct academician of the Academy; as academician-administrator of Hall of Heavenly Pattern was prefect of Yingtian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From Diarist he was elevated to Drafting Official of the Central Secretariat and direct academician of the Academy, and as academician-administrator of the Hall of Heavenly Pattern governed Yingtian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 董敦逸、黃廷基摭升過，改集賢院學士。

translations.literal: Dong Dunyi and Huang Tingji collected Sheng's faults; changed to Academic Gentlemen of Collecting Writings Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Dunyi and Huang Tingji collected Sheng's faults, and he was reassigned as Academic Gentlemen of the Collecting Writings Hall.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，翟思、張商英又劾之，削職，知房州、歸州；

translations.literal: Early Shaosheng, Zhai Si and Zhang Shangying again impeached him; office stripped; prefect of Fangzhou and Guizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaosheng era Zhai Si and Zhang Shangying again impeached him. His office was stripped and he was made prefect of Fangzhou and Guizhou;

sentences.zh: 貶水部員外郎，分司；

translations.literal: demoted to Vice Director of Waterways, branch service;
translations.idiomatic: he was demoted to Vice Director of Waterways with branch service;

sentences.zh: 又貶果州團練副使，汀州安置。

translations.literal: again demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Guozhou, residence at Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and again demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Guozhou, with residence ordered at Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: Died at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 升在元祐初，嘗言：「王安石擅名世之學，為一代文宗。

translations.literal: Early Yuanyou Sheng once said: "Wang Anshi monopolized learning famous in the world and was a literary patriarch of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era Sheng once said, "Wang Anshi monopolized the learning famous throughout the world and was the literary patriarch of a generation.

sentences.zh: 及進居大位，出其私智，以蓋天下之聰明，遂為大害。

translations.literal: When he advanced to high position he brought out his private wisdom to cover the empire's intelligence—thus becoming a great harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he rose to high office he brought out his private wisdom to blanket the empire's intelligence, and thus became a great harm.

sentences.zh: 今蘇軾文章學問，中外所服，然德業器識，有所不足。

translations.literal: Today Su Shi's literary learning is admired within and without the court, yet in virtue, achievement, capacity, and insight he is somewhat insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Today Su Shi's literary learning is admired within and without the court, yet in virtue, achievement, capacity, and insight he is somewhat lacking.

sentences.zh: 為翰林學士，已極其任矣；

translations.literal: As Hanlin Academician he has already reached the limit of that appointment;
translations.idiomatic: As Hanlin Academician he has already reached the limit of that office;

sentences.zh: 若使輔佐經綸，願以安石為戒。」

translations.literal: if he were made to assist in governance, I pray take Anshi as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: if he were set to assist in governance, I pray the court take Anshi as a warning."

sentences.zh: 世譏其失言。

translations.literal: The world mocked his misplaced words.
translations.idiomatic: The world mocked him for his misplaced words.

sentences.zh: 韓川，字元伯，陝人。

translations.literal: Han Chuan, courtesy name Yuanbo, a man of Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chuan, courtesy name Yuanbo, was a man of Shaan.

sentences.zh: 進士上第，歷開封府推官。

translations.literal: Passed jinshi at the top; served as judicial officer of Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination at the top of his class and served as judicial officer of Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，用劉摯薦，為監察御史。

translations.literal: Early Yuanyou, on Liu Zhi's recommendation, he became Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era, on Liu Zhi's recommendation, he became Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 極論市易之害，以為：「雖曰平均物直，而其實不免貨交以取利，就使有獲，尚不可為，況所獲不如所亡，果何事也？

translations.literal: He argued exhaustively the harm of the Market Exchange Law, saying: "Though it is called averaging market value, in fact it does not avoid commodity exchange to take profit; even if there were gain it still should not be done—how much less when gain does not equal loss—what in the end is the matter?
translations.idiomatic: He argued at length against the harm of the Market Exchange Law, saying, "Though it is called averaging market value, in fact it does not avoid commodity exchange to seize profit. Even if there were gain, the law still should not stand—how much less when what is gained does not equal what is lost. What, in the end, is the point of it?

sentences.zh: 願量留官吏，與之期，使趣罷此法。」

translations.literal: I hope to measure retaining officials, set a deadline with them, and hasten abolition of this law."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the court measure how many officials to retain, set them a deadline, and hasten the abolition of this law."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Promoted to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「朝廷於人才，常欲推至公以博采，及其弊也，則幾於利權勢而抑孤寒；

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The court toward talent often wishes to promote utmost fairness to gather broadly; when it goes wrong it nearly favors power and suppresses the isolated and poor;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Toward talent the court often wishes to promote utmost fairness and gather men broadly; yet when the system goes wrong it nearly favors power and suppresses the isolated and poor;

sentences.zh: 常欲收勤績以赴用，要其終也，則莫不收虛名而廢實效。

translations.literal: often wishes to gather diligent achievement for employment; at the end it only gathers empty fame and casts aside real effect.
translations.idiomatic: it often wishes to gather diligent achievement for employment, yet in the end it only gathers empty reputation and casts aside real effect.

sentences.zh: 近制太中大夫以上歲舉守臣，遇大州闕，則選諸所表；

translations.literal: Recent regulation: Grandees of Palace Attendance and above annually recommend circuit administrators; when a great prefecture falls vacant they select from all submitted lists;
translations.idiomatic: Under recent regulation, Grandees of Palace Attendance and above annually recommend circuit administrators; when a great prefecture falls vacant, the court selects from all submitted lists;

sentences.zh: 他雖考課上等，皆莫得預。

translations.literal: others though in evaluation upper grade still may not participate.
translations.idiomatic: others who rank upper in evaluation still may not compete.

sentences.zh: 推原旨意，固欲得人。

translations.literal: Tracing the original intent, it surely is to get capable men.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the original intent, the rule surely aims to secure capable men.

sentences.zh: 然所謂太中大夫以上，率在京師，諸馳騖請求者，得之為易；

translations.literal: Yet those called Grandees and above are mostly in the capital; those who hustle and plead obtain posts easily;
translations.idiomatic: Yet those titled Grandee of Palace Attendance and above are mostly in the capital; men who hustle and plead obtain posts easily;

sentences.zh: 至於淹歷郡縣治狀應法者，顧出其下，則是謹身修潔之人，不若營求一章之速化也。」

translations.literal: as for those who have served long in prefectures and counties with performance meeting standards, they are placed below—then those careful in conduct and cultivation are not equal to one memorial from the ambitious for swift advancement."
translations.idiomatic: while those who have long served in prefectures and counties with performance that meets the standards are placed below them. Thus the man careful in conduct and cultivation is not equal to one memorial from the ambitious office-seeker for swift advancement."

sentences.zh: 於是詔吏部更立法。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to revise the law.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to revise the law.

sentences.zh: 張舜民論西夏事，乞停封冊，朝廷以為開邊隙，罷其御史。

translations.literal: Zhang Shunmin discussed Western Xia affairs, begging to halt enfeoffment; the court thought it opened border disputes and dismissed his censor's post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shunmin discussed Western Xia affairs and begged that enfeoffment be halted. The court thought this would open border disputes and dismissed him from his censor's post.

sentences.zh: 梁燾等為舜民爭之。

translations.literal: Liang Dao and others contended for Shunmin.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Dao and others contended on Shunmin's behalf.

sentences.zh: 川與呂陶、上官均謂舜民之言，實不可行。

translations.literal: Chuan with Lü Tao and Shangguan Jun said Shunmin's words in truth could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan, together with Lü Tao and Shangguan Jun, said that in truth Shunmin's words could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 燾等去，川亦改太常少卿，不拜，加集賢校理、知潁州。

translations.literal: When Dao and others left, Chuan too was changed to Vice Director of Court of Imperial Sacrifices; did not accept; added collation at Collecting Writings; prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao and the others left office, Chuan too was reassigned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He did not accept the post and was instead given collation at the Collecting Writings Hall and made prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 還為侍御史、樞密都承旨，進中書舍人、吏、禮二部侍郎，以龍圖閣待制復守潁，徙虢州。

translations.literal: Returned as Attending Censor and Director of Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner's Court; advanced to Drafting Official, Vice Ministers of Personnel and Rites; as Dragon Diagram academician-administrator again guarded Ying; transferred to Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Attending Censor and Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner's Court, advanced to Drafting Official and Vice Minister of Personnel and of Rites, and as academician-administrator of the Dragon Diagram Hall again governed Ying; he was later transferred to Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 與孫升同受責，由坊州、郢州貶屯田員外郎，分司，岷州團練副使，道州安置。

translations.literal: With Sun Sheng he received the same punishment—from Fangzhou and Yingzhou demoted to Vice Director of Farms branch service, Vice Military Training Commissioner of Minzhou, residence at Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Sun Sheng he received the same punishment: from Fangzhou and Yingzhou he was demoted to Vice Director of Farms with branch service, then to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Minzhou, with residence ordered at Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，得故官，知青、襄 二州，卒。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended, restored former office; prefect of Qing and Xiang prefectures; died.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended the throne, Chuan was restored to his former offices and governed Qing and Xiang; he then died.

sentences.zh: 龔鼎臣

translations.literal: Gong Dingchen
translations.idiomatic: Gong Dingchen

sentences.zh: 龔鼎臣，字輔之，鄆之須城人。

translations.literal: Gong Dingchen, courtesy name Fuzhi, of Xucheng in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Dingchen, courtesy name Fuzhi, was from Xucheng in Yan.

sentences.zh: 父誘衷，武陵令。

translations.literal: His father Youzhong, magistrate of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Youzhong had been magistrate of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣幼孤自立，景祐元年第進士，為平陰主簿，疏泄瀦水，得良田數百千頃。

translations.literal: Dingchen was orphaned young and stood on his own; in the first year of Jingyou he passed jinshi; was chief clerk of Pingyin; drained the flooded pond, obtaining several hundred thousand qing of good fields.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen lost his father young and stood on his own. In the first year of Jingyou he passed the jinshi examination and served as chief clerk of Pingyin, where he drained a flooded pond and reclaimed several hundred thousand qing of good farmland.

sentences.zh: 調孟州司法參軍，以薦，為泰寧軍節度掌書記。

translations.literal: Transferred to judicial aide of Mengzhou; on recommendation became secretary to the Taizhou military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to judicial aide of Mengzhou and, on recommendation, became secretary to the Taizhou military governor.

sentences.zh: 徂徠石介死，讒者謂介北走遼，詔兗州劾狀。

translations.literal: When Cui Lai Shi Jie died, slanderers said Jie had fled north to Liao; an edict ordered Yanzhou to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jie of Cui Lai died, slanderers said Jie had fled north to Liao. An edict ordered Yanzhou to investigate.

sentences.zh: 郡守杜衍會問，掾屬莫對，鼎臣獨曰：「介寧有是，願以闔門證其死。」

translations.literal: Prefect Du Yan convened the inquiry; no clerk answered; only Dingchen said: "Would Jie have done this? I offer my entire household to prove his death."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Du Yan convened the inquiry. None of the clerks would answer until Dingchen alone said, "Would Jie have done such a thing? I stake my entire household on proving his death."

sentences.zh: 衍探懷出奏稿示之，曰：「吾既保介矣，君年少見義如是，未可量也。」

translations.literal: Yan drew from his breast the memorial draft and showed him: "I have already vouched for Jie; you are young and see righteousness thus—the measure of you cannot yet be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Yan drew from his breast the memorial draft and showed it to him, saying, "I have already vouched for Jie. You are young, yet you see righteousness like this—your measure cannot yet be taken."

sentences.zh: 舉為秘書省著作佐郎、知萊蕪縣。

translations.literal: Recommended as Assistant in the Secretariat; magistrate of Laowu.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as Assistant in the Secretariat and became magistrate of Laowu.

sentences.zh: 大臣薦試館職，坐與石介善，不召。

translations.literal: Great ministers recommended trial for palace post; because he was friendly with Shi Jie, he was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers recommended him for trial appointment to a palace post, but because he had been friendly with Shi Jie he was not summoned.

sentences.zh: 徙知濛陽縣，轉秘書丞。

translations.literal: Transferred magistrate of Mengyang; promoted to Secretariat assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Mengyang and promoted to Secretariat assistant.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，知安丘縣。

translations.literal: Mourning for mother; when mourning ended, magistrate of Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he entered mourning; when mourning ended he became magistrate of Anqiu.

sentences.zh: 以賢良方正召試秘閣，轉太常博士，賜五品服，知渠州。

translations.literal: Summoned for erudite and upright examination at Secret Archive; transferred Doctor of Court of Imperial Sacrifices; granted fifth-rank robes; prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned for the erudite-and-upright examination at the Secret Archive, transferred to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granted fifth-rank robes, and made prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 渠故僻陋無學者，鼎臣請於朝，建廟學，選邑子為生，日講說，立課肄法，人大勸，始有登科者。

translations.literal: Qu was formerly remote and had no scholars; Dingchen requested of the court to build a prefectural school, select district sons as students, lecture daily, establish curriculum and study methods—the people were greatly encouraged; there were first those who passed the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou had formerly been remote and without scholars. Dingchen requested permission to build a prefectural school, select sons of the district as students, lecture daily, and establish curriculum and methods of study. The people were greatly encouraged, and for the first time candidates from Quzhou passed the examinations.

sentences.zh: 郡人繪像事之。

translations.literal: The prefectural people painted his image to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture painted his image to honor him.

sentences.zh: 召入編校史館書籍，轉都官，擢起居舍人、同知諫院。

translations.literal: Summoned to compile books in the History Office; transferred to Ministry of Revenue directorate; elevated to Diarist-of-the-Left and concurrent vice director of Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to compile books in the History Office, transferred to a directorship in the Ministry of Revenue, and elevated to Diarist-of-the-Left with concurrent appointment as vice director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 歲冬旱，將錫春宴，鼎臣曰：「旱甾太甚，非君臣同樂之時，請罷宴以答天戒。」

translations.literal: Winter drought that year; the court was about to grant the spring banquet; Dingchen said: "Drought disaster is too great—not a time for ruler and ministers to rejoice together; I ask to cancel the banquet to answer Heaven's warning."
translations.idiomatic: That winter there was drought. The court was about to grant the spring banquet when Dingchen said, "The drought disaster is too severe—this is no time for ruler and ministers to rejoice together. I ask that the banquet be canceled to answer Heaven's warning."

sentences.zh: 日當食，陰雲不見，鼎臣曰：「陽精既虧，四方必見，為異益大，願精思力行，進賢遠佞，以應皇極。」

translations.literal: On the day of an eclipse, yin clouds did not appear; Dingchen said: "The yang essence is already depleted—the four quarters will surely see it; the anomaly is still greater; I hope for refined thought and earnest conduct, advancing the worthy and distancing the fawning, to respond to the imperial pole."
translations.idiomatic: On the day of an eclipse the yin clouds did not appear. Dingchen said, "The yang essence is already depleted—the four quarters will surely take note; the omen is all the greater. I hope for refined thought and earnest conduct, advancing the worthy and distancing the fawning, to answer the imperial pole."

sentences.zh: 又論內侍都知鄧保信罪狀，不應出入禁中；

translations.literal: He also argued the crimes of inner-attendant chief Deng Baoxin—not fit to enter and leave the forbidden palace;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued the crimes of the inner-attendant chief Deng Baoxin, saying he was unfit to enter and leave the forbidden palace;

sentences.zh: 蘇安靜年未五十，不應超押班；

translations.literal: Su Anjing is not yet fifty—not fit to leap over and lead the class.
translations.idiomatic: and that Su Anjing, not yet fifty, was unfit to leap over his seniors and lead the class.

sentences.zh: 妃嬪贈三代，僭后禮；

translations.literal: Consorts and concubines were granted posthumous honors for three generations, usurping the rites due a queen;
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and concubines were granted posthumous honors for three generations, usurping the rites of a queen;

sentences.zh: 董淑妃賜諡，非是；

translations.literal: to bestow a posthumous title on Lady Dong the Pure Consort was wrong;
translations.idiomatic: to grant a posthumous title to Pure Consort Dong was improper;

sentences.zh: 凡大禮赦，請準太平興國詔書，前期下禁約，後有犯不原，以杜指赦為姦者，宜著為令；

translations.literal: for every great amnesty, he asked that the Taiping Xingguo edict be followed—prohibitions issued beforehand, offenders afterward not pardoned, to cut off those who counted on amnesty to do evil—and that this be written into statute;
translations.idiomatic: on every great amnesty he asked that the court follow the Taiping Xingguo precedent: prohibitions issued in advance, no pardon afterward for violators, to shut off those who banked on clemency to do wrong—and that this be enacted as law;

sentences.zh: 開封三司於法外斷獄，朝廷多曲徇其請，願先付中書審畫。

translations.literal: the Kaifeng Three Offices tried cases beyond the code, and the court often bent to their requests; he wished them first sent to the Secretariat for review.
translations.idiomatic: the Kaifeng Three Offices judged cases outside the statutes, and the court often indulged their requests; he asked that such matters first be sent to the Secretariat for review.

sentences.zh: 仁宗悉從之。

translations.literal: Renzong accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong accepted every proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋兼管勾國子監，判登聞檢院，詳定寬恤民力奏議。

translations.literal: Soon he also supervised the Directorate of Education and judged the Palace Memorial Appeals Office, and worked through memorials on lenient measures to spare the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also supervised the Directorate of Education, judged the Palace Memorial Appeals Office, and worked through memorials on lenient policies to ease the people's burdens.

sentences.zh: 淮南災，以鼎臣體量安撫，蠲逋振貸，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: When Huainan suffered disaster, Dingchen was sent to assess and console; he remitted arrears and extended relief loans, saving a great many lives.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was stricken, Dingchen was sent to investigate and console the region; he remitted tax arrears and extended relief loans, preserving countless lives.

sentences.zh: 為遼正旦使，鼎臣奏：「景德中，遼犯淄、青，臣祖母、兄、姊皆見略，義不忍往。」

translations.literal: As envoy to Liao for the New Year's audience, Dingchen memorialized: "In the Jingde era Liao raided Zi and Qing; my grandmother, elder brother, and elder sister were all taken. In righteousness I cannot bear to go."
translations.idiomatic: When named envoy to Liao for the New Year's audience, Dingchen memorialized, "In the Jingde era Liao invaded Zi and Qing; my grandmother, elder brother, and elder sister were all carried off. In duty I cannot bear to go."

sentences.zh: 許之，仍詔後子孫並免行焉。

translations.literal: Permission was granted, and an edict further exempted his descendants from such missions.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented, and further decreed that his descendants in turn should be exempt from such embassies.

sentences.zh: 俄拜戶部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事，賜三品服。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and was granted third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, with third-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 轉吏、禮二部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director in the Ministries of Personnel and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director in the Ministries of Personnel and of Rites.

sentences.zh: 論宗室宜歲試補外官，請汰濫官冗兵，蕃財用，禁奢靡。

translations.literal: He argued that members of the imperial clan should be examined yearly before receiving outside office; he asked to weed out superfluous posts and redundant troops, husband the treasury, and forbid extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that imperial clansmen be examined annually before filling outside posts; he asked to cut superfluous offices and idle troops, husband state funds, and forbid luxury.

sentences.zh: 連劾薛向姦暴，鬻鹽、市馬皆罔上。

translations.literal: He repeatedly impeached Xue Xiang for cruelty and violence; his salt monopoly and horse purchases had all deceived the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly impeached Xue Xiang for cruelty and rapacity; monopolizing salt and buying horses, Xiang had deceived the throne throughout.

sentences.zh: 英宗登位，屢乞延訪臣下，親決國事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Dingchen repeatedly begged that he extend frequent audiences to his ministers and decide state affairs in person.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Dingchen repeatedly begged him to summon his ministers often and decide state affairs himself.

sentences.zh: 上疏勸皇太后早還政；

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial urging the Empress Dowager to return power early;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized urging the Empress Dowager to restore the regency to the emperor without delay;

sentences.zh: 及卷簾而御璽未復，又極論。

translations.literal: when she drew the curtain to hold court yet the imperial seal had not been restored, he argued the point again at length.
translations.idiomatic: when she held court from behind the curtain while the imperial seal had not yet been returned, he argued the matter again at length.

sentences.zh: 謂昭陵宜儉葬，景靈神御殿不宜增侈，以彰先帝恭德。

translations.literal: He said the Zhaoling tomb ought to be buried frugally and the Spirit Hall of Jingling ought not be enlarged in splendor, to display the late emperor's humble virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He held that Zhaoling should be buried frugally and the Spirit Hall at Jingling should not be enlarged, thereby displaying the late emperor's modest virtue.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣在言路累歲，闊 略細故，至大事，無所顧忌。

translations.literal: Dingchen spent years on the remonstrance path, broad and careless over small matters, yet on great affairs he spared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen spent years on the remonstrance path, broad-minded over trifles, yet on great affairs he held back nothing.

sentences.zh: 然其言優遊和平，不為峻激，使人主易聽，退亦未嘗語人，故其事多施行。

translations.literal: Yet his words were easy and measured, never harsh or inflammatory, so that the sovereign could readily heed them; when he withdrew he never spoke of them to others, and therefore most of his proposals were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his words were measured and calm, never sharp or inflammatory, so the sovereign could readily hear them; in retirement he never spoke of them to others, and thus most of what he urged was enacted.

sentences.zh: 改集賢殿修撰、知應天府，徙江寧。

translations.literal: He was changed to Compiler in the Hall for Cherishing Literature and made prefect of Yingtian; later he was transferred to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Compiler in the Hall for Cherishing Literature and prefect of Yingtian, then transferred to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 召還，判太常寺兼禮儀事。

translations.literal: Recalled, he judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently handled ritual affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On recall he judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently handled ritual matters.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，判吏部流內銓、太常寺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Dingchen judged the Ministry of Personnel's roster of internal appointments and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Dingchen judged the Ministry of Personnel's roster of internal appointments and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 選人得官，待班謝辭，率皆留滯。

translations.literal: Candidates who received office often lingered waiting to take leave and offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Those who received appointment often lingered, waiting to take leave and offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣奏易為門謝辭，甚便之。

translations.literal: Dingchen memorialized that it would be far easier if thanks were offered at the gate; the change proved very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen memorialized that thanks at the gate would be far easier; the change proved greatly convenient.

sentences.zh: 明堂議侑帝，或云以真宗，或云以仁宗。

translations.literal: In the debate over who should receive sacrifice beside the emperor at the Bright Hall, some said Zhenzong, others Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Bright Hall debate over the accompanying sacrifice, some urged Zhenzong, others Renzong.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣 曰：“嚴父莫大於配天，未聞以祖也。”

translations.literal: Dingchen said, "Honoring the father reaches its height in matching Heaven; I have never heard of matching one's grandfather."
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen said, "To honor the father reaches its height in matching Heaven; never yet have I heard of matching the grandfather."

sentences.zh: 乃奉英宗配。

translations.literal: Accordingly Yingzong was offered as the match.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Emperor Yingzong was paired in the rite.

sentences.zh: 王安石侍講，欲賜坐。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi lectured before the throne, he wished to be granted a seat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi lectured before the throne, he asked to be granted a seat.

sentences.zh: 事下禮官，鼎臣言不可，安石不悅。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ritual officials; Dingchen said it could not be done, and Anshi was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the ritual officials; Dingchen said it could not be allowed, and Anshi took offense.

sentences.zh: 求補外，知兗州。

translations.literal: He asked for an outside post and was made prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sought an outside appointment and was made prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸道方田使者希功賞，概取稅虛額及嘗所蠲者，加舊籍以病民。

translations.literal: At the time the field-tax commissioners in the circuits, eager for merit and reward, broadly took inflated tax quotas and amounts once remitted, adding them back to the old registers to burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the time circuit commissioners for equalizing the fields, hungry for merit and reward, broadly seized inflated tax quotas and levies once remitted, restoring them to the old registers to afflict the people.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣獨按籍差次為十等，一無所增，兗人德之。

translations.literal: Dingchen alone followed the registers and ranked households in ten grades, increasing nothing; the people of Yanzhou were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen alone followed the registers and ranked households in ten grades without adding a single levy; the people of Yanzhou blessed him.

sentences.zh: 改吏部，提舉西京崇福宮。

translations.literal: Changed to the Ministry of Personnel, made intendant of the Western Capital's Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and made intendant of the Chongfu Palace in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 復判太常寺，留守南京。

translations.literal: He again judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and remained at Nanjing as regent.
translations.idiomatic: He again judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and stayed at Nanjing as regent.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，神宗顧語移晷，喜曰：「人言卿老不任事，精明乃爾，行且用卿矣。」

translations.literal: On taking leave at court, Shenzong spoke with him a long while and said with pleasure, "Men say you are old and unfit for office, yet your clarity is such as this—you will soon be employed again."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience Shenzong spoke with him at length and said gladly, "Men say you are old and unfit for office, yet see how keen you are—you will soon be used again."

sentences.zh: 鄭穆，字閎中，福州侯官人。

translations.literal: Zheng Mu, styled Hongzhong, was a man of Houguan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mu, courtesy name Hongzhong, was a native of Houguan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 性醇謹好學，讀書至忘櫛沐，進退容止必以禮。

translations.literal: By nature he was earnest, careful, and fond of learning; in reading he would forget to comb or bathe, and in advancing or withdrawing his bearing was always according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Earnest and careful by nature, he loved learning; in study he would forget to comb his hair or bathe, and whether coming or going his bearing always followed ritual.

sentences.zh: 門人千數，與陳襄、陳烈、周希孟友，號「四先生」。

translations.literal: His disciples numbered in the thousands; with Chen Xiang, Chen Lie, and Zhou Ximeng he was friends, and together they were called the "Four Masters."
translations.idiomatic: His disciples numbered in the thousands; with Chen Xiang, Chen Lie, and Zhou Ximeng he formed a circle styled the "Four Masters."

sentences.zh: 舉進士，四冠鄉書，遂登第， 為壽安主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examinations with top honors four times, then entered the jinshi rolls and was appointed registrar of Shou'an.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the provincial lists four times, then passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Shou'an.

sentences.zh: 召為國子監直講，除編校集賢院書籍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as lecturer in the Directorate of Education and made collator of books in the Hall for Assembling Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as lecturer in the Directorate of Education and made collator in the Hall for Assembling Worthies.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，為館閣校勘，積官太常博士。

translations.literal: When his term ended he became reviser in the palace library and rose by degrees to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he became reviser in the palace library and rose step by step to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 乞納一秩，先南郊追封考妣，從之。

translations.literal: He asked to surrender one rank so that at the next suburban sacrifice his parents might receive posthumous ennoblement; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to surrender one rank so that at the next suburban sacrifice his father and mother might receive posthumous ennoblement; the court granted it.

sentences.zh: 改集賢校理，求外補，通判汾州。

translations.literal: He was made collator in the Hall for Assembling Worthies, sought an outside post, and was made transit vice-prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Made collator in the Hall for Assembling Worthies, he sought an outside post and was appointed transit vice-prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，召為岐王侍講。

translations.literal: In Xining year three he was summoned as lecturer to the Prince of Qi's household.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining he was summoned as lecturer to the Prince of Qi's household.

sentences.zh: 嘉王出閣，改諸王侍講。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jia left the palace school, Mu was changed to lecturer for the princes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jia left the inner palace school, Mu was reassigned as lecturer to the princes.

sentences.zh: 府僚闕員，御史陳襄請擇人，神宗曰：「如鄭穆德行，乃宜左右王者。」

translations.literal: When a staff post in the princely mansion fell vacant, Remonstrance Officer Chen Xiang asked that a man be chosen; Shenzong said, "A man of Zheng Mu's conduct is fit to stand beside a king."
translations.idiomatic: When a post in the princely household fell vacant, Remonstrance Officer Chen Xiang asked that someone be chosen; Shenzong said, "One of Zheng Mu's character is fit to attend a prince."

sentences.zh: 凡居館閣三十年，而在王邸一紀，非公事不及執政之門。

translations.literal: In all he spent thirty years in the palace library, and twelve years in the princely mansions, never visiting the chief ministers' doors except on public business.
translations.idiomatic: He spent thirty years in the palace library and twelve years in the princely mansions, never calling at the chief ministers' gates except on public business.

sentences.zh: 講說有法，可為勸戒者，必反復擿誦，岐、喜二王咸敬禮焉。

translations.literal: His lecturing had method; whatever could serve as warning or admonition he would repeat and recite again and again, and the Princes of Qi and Xi both treated him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: His teaching had method; whatever could warn or admonish he would repeat and recite again and again, and the Princes of Qi and Xi both honored him.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，出知越州，加朝散大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng he went out as prefect of Yuezhou and was promoted to Grandee of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng he was sent out as prefect of Yuezhou and promoted to Grandee of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 先是，鑒湖旱乾，民因田其中，延袤百里，官籍而稅之。

translations.literal: Earlier Mirror Lake had dried in drought, and the people had taken fields within it, stretching a hundred li; the government registered the land and taxed it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Mirror Lake had dried in drought and the people had farmed its bed for a hundred li; the government registered the land and taxed it.

sentences.zh: 既而連年水溢，民逋官租積萬緡，穆奏免之。

translations.literal: Then for years the waters rose; the people owed official rent amounting to tens of thousands of strings, and Mu memorialized for remission.
translations.idiomatic: Then for years the waters rose; the people owed official rent in tens of thousands of strings, and Mu memorialized for remission.

sentences.zh: 未滿告老，管勾杭州洞霄宮。

translations.literal: His term not yet complete, he memorialized to retire and was put in charge of Hangzhou's Cave of the Azure Sky.
translations.idiomatic: Before his term ended he petitioned to retire and was put in charge of the Cave of the Azure Sky at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，召拜國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the opening of the Yuanyou era he was summoned and appointed Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanyou era he was summoned and made Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 每講益，無問寒暑，雖童子必朝服廷接，以禮送迎。

translations.literal: Whenever he lectured on the Book of Changes he did so regardless of heat or cold; even boys he received in court dress in the hall, seeing them off with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he lectured on the Book of Changes he did so in heat or cold alike; even boys he received in court dress in the hall and sent away with ritual courtesy.

sentences.zh: 諸生皆尊其經術，服其教訓。

translations.literal: The students all honored his classical learning and submitted to his instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The students all revered his classical learning and submitted to his instruction.

sentences.zh: 故人張景晟者死，遣白金五百兩，託其孤，穆曰：「恤孤，吾事也，金於何有？」

translations.literal: An old friend, Zhang Jingsheng, on dying left five hundred taels of white silver, entrusting his orphan to Mu; Mu said, "To comfort the orphan is my affair—what need is there for gold?"
translations.idiomatic: His old friend Zhang Jingsheng, on dying, left five hundred taels of silver, entrusting his orphan to Mu; Mu said, "To comfort the orphan is my duty—what need is there for gold?"

sentences.zh: 反金而收其子，長之。

translations.literal: He returned the gold and took in the son, raising him to adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the gold and took in the boy, raising him to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 三年，揚王、荊王請為侍講，罷祭酒，除直集賢院，復入王府。

translations.literal: In the third year the Princes of Yang and Jing asked that he serve as their lecturer; he was removed as Director and made drafter in the Hall for Assembling Worthies, returning to the princely mansions.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Princes of Yang and Jing asked that he lecture for them; he was removed as Director, made drafter in the Hall for Assembling Worthies, and returned to the princely mansions.

sentences.zh: 荊王薨，為揚王翊善。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jing died, he served as tutor to the Prince of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jing died, he became tutor to the Prince of Yang.

sentences.zh: 太學生乞為師，復除祭酒，兼徐王翊善。

translations.literal: Students of the Imperial University begged that he be their teacher; he was again made Director and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Imperial University petitioned that he be their teacher; he was again made Director and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜給事中兼祭酒；

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Supervising Secretary and concurrently Director;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Supervising Secretary and concurrently Director;

sentences.zh: 五年，除寶文閣待制，仍祭酒。

translations.literal: in the fifth year he was made Awaiting-Appointment Drafter of the Pavilion of Treasured Literature, still serving as Director.
translations.idiomatic: in the fifth year he was made Awaiting-Appointment Drafter of the Pavilion of Treasured Literature while still serving as Director.

sentences.zh: 六年，請老，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he requested old age and was made intendant of the Cave of the Azure Sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he asked to retire and was made intendant of the Cave of the Azure Sky.

sentences.zh: 敕過門下，給事中范祖禹言：「穆雖年出七十，精力尚強。

translations.literal: When the edict passed the Secretariat, Supervising Secretary Fan Zuyu said, "Though Mu is past seventy, his vigor is still strong.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict passed the Secretariat, Supervising Secretary Fan Zuyu said, "Though Mu is past seventy, his strength is still firm.

sentences.zh: 古者大夫七十而致仕，有不得謝，則賜之几杖。

translations.literal: In antiquity a grandee at seventy would retire; if he could not be released, the throne would grant him a folding stool and staff.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a grandee at seventy would retire; if leave to withdraw was denied, the throne would grant him a folding stool and staff.

sentences.zh: 祭酒居師資之地，正宜處老成，願毋輕聽其去。」

translations.literal: The Director's post is the seat of the teacher; it is precisely the place for a man of seasoned age—I beg that his departure not be lightly granted."
translations.idiomatic: The Director's post is the seat of the teacher; it is precisely where a man of seasoned years should stand—I beg that his departure not be lightly granted."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no reply.
