translations.idiomatic: The court did not answer.

sentences.zh: 太學之士數千人，以狀詣司業，又詣宰相請留，亦不從。

translations.literal: Several thousand students of the Imperial University submitted a petition to the Vice Director and then to the chief minister asking that he be kept; again they were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Imperial University students petitioned the Vice Director and then the chief minister to keep him; again they were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 於是公卿大夫各為詩贈其行。

translations.literal: Thereupon the grandees and high officials each made a poem to present at his departure.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon grandees and high officials each composed a poem to send him on his way.

sentences.zh: 空學出祖汴東門外，都人觀者如堵，歎未嘗見。

translations.literal: Students of the Imperial University escorted him out to offer a farewell beyond the eastern gate of Bian; townspeople who came to watch packed the roads, sighing that they had never seen the like.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial University students escorted him to a farewell beyond the eastern gate of Bian; the watching crowd packed the roads, sighing that they had never seen the like.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died, aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 子璆，軍事推官。

translations.literal: His son Qiu was a military judicial officer.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiu served as a military judicial officer.

sentences.zh: 席旦，字晉仲，河南人。

translations.literal: Xi Dan, styled Jinzhong, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Dan, courtesy name Jinzhong, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 七歲能詩，嘗登沉黎嶺，得句警拔，觀者驚異。

translations.literal: At seven he could compose poetry; once climbing Mount Chenli he produced lines so striking that onlookers marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could compose verse; once climbing Mount Chenli he produced lines so striking that onlookers marveled.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，舉進士，禮部不奏名。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng era he passed the jinshi examination, but the Ministry of Rites did not report his name.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanfeng era he passed the jinshi examination, but the Ministry of Rites did not enter his name on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 時方求邊功，旦詣闕上書言：「戰勝易，守勝難，知所以得之，必知所以守之。」

translations.literal: As the court then sought merit on the frontier, Dan went to the capital and submitted a memorial saying, "Victory in battle is easy; victory in holding is hard. One who knows how to win must know how to hold."
translations.idiomatic: As the court then sought merit on the frontier, Dan went to the capital and memorialized, "Victory in battle is easy; victory in holding is hard. Who knows how to win must know how to hold."

sentences.zh: 神宗嘉納，令廷試賜第。

translations.literal: Shenzong praised and received it and ordered a palace examination with bestowal of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong praised and accepted it and ordered a palace examination with conferral of rank.

sentences.zh: 歷齊州司法參軍、鄭州河陽教授、敕令所刪定官。

translations.literal: He successively served as judicial adjutant of Qizhou, instructor at Heyang in Zhengzhou, and reviser in the Edict-Compiling Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial adjutant of Qizhou, instructor at Heyang in Zhengzhou, and reviser of edicts in the Office for Compiling Statutes.

sentences.zh: 徽宗召對，擢右正言，遷右司諫。

translations.literal: Huizong summoned him for audience and promoted him to Right Remonstrance Officer, then Right Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong summoned him for audience and promoted him to Right Remonstrance Officer, then to Right Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞錢遹率同列請廢元祐皇后而冊劉氏為太后，旦面質為不可。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Qian Kui led his colleagues in asking that the Yuanyou Empress be deposed and Lady Liu be installed as Empress Dowager; Dan confronted him to his face that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Qian Kui led his colleagues in asking that the Yuanyou Empress be deposed and Lady Liu installed as Empress Dowager; Dan confronted him face to face that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 遹劾旦陰佐元祐之政，左轉吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: Kui impeached Dan for secretly assisting Yuanyou governance and had him transferred left to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Kui impeached Dan for secretly aiding Yuanyou policies and had him demoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 改太常少卿，遷中書舍人、給事中。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat and Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat and Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 新建殿中省，命為監，俄拜御史中丞兼侍講。

translations.literal: When the Palace Directorate was newly built he was ordered as its intendant, and soon was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and concurrently lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Palace Directorate was newly established he was appointed its intendant, and soon was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and concurrently lecturer.

sentences.zh: 內侍郝隨驕橫，旦劾罷之，都人誦其直。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Hao Sui was arrogant and overbearing; Dan impeached and removed him, and the capital sang of his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Hao Sui was arrogant and overbearing; Dan impeached him and had him removed, and the capital praised his uprightness.

sentences.zh: 帝以其章有「媚惑先帝」之語，嫌為指斥，旋改吏部侍郎，以顯謨閣待制知宣州。

translations.literal: The emperor, because his memorial contained the phrase "bewitching the late emperor," thought it a personal attack and soon transferred him to Vice Minister of Personnel and made him Awaiting-Appointment Drafter of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because his memorial contained the phrase "bewitching the late emperor," took it as a personal attack and soon transferred him to Vice Minister of Personnel and made him Awaiting-Appointment Drafter of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部侍郎，還吏部。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue and again returned to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue and returned to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 郝隨復入侍，乃以顯謨閣直學士知成都府。

translations.literal: When Hao Sui again entered to attend, Dan was made Direct Drafter of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao Sui again entered attendance, Dan was made Direct Drafter of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 自趙諗以狂謀誅後，蜀數有妖言，議者遂言蜀土習亂。

translations.literal: After Zhao Shen was put to death for his mad plot, Shu repeatedly had demonic talk; deliberators then said the land of Shu was habituated to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Shen was executed for his mad plot, Shu repeatedly had ominous rumors; deliberators then said the people of Shu were prone to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 或導旦治以峻猛，旦政和平，徙鄭州。

translations.literal: Some guided Dan to govern with severity and harshness; Dan's government was peaceful and mild, and he was moved to Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Dan to govern with severity and harshness; Dan's rule was mild and peaceful, and he was transferred to Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 入見，言：「蜀人性善柔，自古稱兵背叛，皆非其土俗，願勿為慮。」

translations.literal: On audience he said, "The people of Shu are by nature gentle and yielding; from antiquity those who took up arms in rebellion were none of them following local custom—I beg that Your Majesty not worry."
translations.idiomatic: On audience he said, "The people of Shu are by nature gentle and yielding; from antiquity those who took up arms in rebellion were none of them following local custom—I beg that Your Majesty give it no thought."

sentences.zh: 遂言：「蜀用鐵錢，以其艱於轉移，故權以楮券，而有司冀贏羨，為之益多，使民不敢信。」

translations.literal: He further said, "Shu uses iron cash; because it is hard to transport, paper notes were temporarily issued in its place; yet the officials hoped for surplus profit and made them ever more numerous, until the people dared not believe."
translations.idiomatic: He then said, "Shu uses iron coin, and because it is hard to move, paper notes were issued as a temporary measure; yet the officials hoped for surplus profit and issued ever more, until the people dared not trust them."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕為卿損數百萬虛券，而別給緡錢與本業，可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Shall I for your sake discard several million in empty notes and separately give strings of cash for the original trades?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shall I void several million in worthless notes for you and separately supply strings of cash for the original trades?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下幸加惠遠民，不愛重費以救敝法，此古聖王用心也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty is pleased to extend favor to distant people and does not love heavy expense in order to save a broken law—this is the heart of the ancient sage-kings."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your Majesty is pleased to show favor to distant people and does not begrudge heavy expense to rescue a broken system—this is the mind of the ancient sage-kings."

sentences.zh: 自是錢引稍仍故。

translations.literal: From this the paper notes gradually followed their former ways.
translations.idiomatic: From this the paper notes gradually returned to their former course.

sentences.zh: 坐進對淹留，黜知滁州。

translations.literal: For lingering too long in audience he was demoted and made prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because he lingered too long in audience he was demoted and made prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝思其治蜀功，復知成都。

translations.literal: After long time the emperor thought on his achievements in governing Shu and again made him prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the emperor recalled his achievements in governing Shu and again made him prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 朝廷開西南夷，黎州守詣幕府白事，言雲南大理國求入朝獻，旦引唐南詔為蜀患，拒卻之。

translations.literal: The court opened the southwestern Yi; the Lizhou prefect came to the headquarters to report matters, saying Dali in Yunnan sought to enter court and offer tribute; Dan cited Tang Nanzhao as a calamity for Shu and refused.
translations.idiomatic: The court opened relations with the southwestern Yi; the prefect of Lizhou came to the headquarters to report that Dali in Yunnan sought to enter court and offer tribute; Dan cited how the Tang's Nanzhao had been a calamity for Shu and refused.

sentences.zh: 已而威州守焦才叔言，欲誘保、霸二州內附。

translations.literal: Soon the Weizhou prefect Jiao Caishu spoke, wishing to entice the inner submission of Ba and Ba prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the prefect of Weizhou, Jiao Caishu, proposed to entice Ba and Ba prefectures to submit inward.

sentences.zh: 旦上章劾才叔為姦利斂困諸蕃之狀，宰相不悅，代以龐恭孫，而徙旦永興。

translations.literal: Dan submitted a memorial impeaching Caishu for wicked profit that oppressed the various tribes; the chief minister was displeased, replaced him with Pang Gongsun, and moved Dan to Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Dan submitted a memorial impeaching Caishu for using wicked profit to oppress the various tribes; the chief minister was displeased, replaced him with Pang Gongsun, and transferred Dan to Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 恭孫俄罪去，加旦述古殿直學士，復知成都。

translations.literal: Gongsun soon left office under charges; Dan was advanced to Direct Drafter of the Hall for Venerating Antiquity and again made prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun soon left office under charges; Dan was promoted to Direct Drafter of the Hall for Venerating Antiquity and again made prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 時郅永壽、湯延俊納土，樞密院用以訹旦，旦曰：「吾以為朝廷悔開疆之禍，今猶自若邪？」

translations.literal: At that time Zhi Yongshou and Tang Yanjun submitted their territories; the Bureau of Military Affairs used this to coax Dan. Dan said: "I thought the court had repented of the disaster of opening new frontiers—are you still the same now?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhi Yongshou and Tang Yanjun surrendered their domains; the Bureau of Military Affairs used the occasion to press Dan. Dan said, "I had thought the court had repented of the calamity of territorial expansion—are you still of the same mind?"

sentences.zh: 力辭之。

translations.literal: He declined with all his force.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 卒於長安，年六十二，贈太中大夫。

translations.literal: He died at Chang'an, age sixty-two, posthumously granted Grandee of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Chang'an, aged sixty-two, and was posthumously granted the title Grandee of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 旦立朝無所附徇，第為中丞時，蔡王似方以疑就第，旦糾其私出府，請推治官吏，議者哂之。

translations.literal: In court Dan attached himself to no faction. Only when he was vice censor-in-chief, Prince Cai Si, because of suspicion, had retired to his mansion; Dan impeached him for leaving the mansion privately and requested that officials be investigated and punished—commentators ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: In court Dan owed allegiance to no faction. Only once, when he was vice censor-in-chief: Prince Cai Si, under suspicion, had retired to his mansion; Dan impeached him for slipping out without leave and asked that the officials involved be investigated and punished—on which commentators only laughed.

sentences.zh: 子益，字大光，紹興初，參知政事。

translations.literal: His son Yi, courtesy name Daguan, at the beginning of the Shaoxing reign became vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, courtesy name Daguan, became vice grand councilor at the opening of the Shaoxing reign.

sentences.zh: 喬執中

translations.literal: Qiao Zhizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhizhong

sentences.zh: 喬執中，字希聖，高郵人。

translations.literal: Qiao Zhizhong, styled Xisheng, was a man of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhizhong, courtesy name Xisheng, was a native of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 入太學，補《五經》講書，五年不謁告。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University, was appointed lecturer on the Five Classics, and for five years never took leave.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University, was appointed lecturer on the Five Classics, and for five years never once requested leave.

sentences.zh: 王安石為群牧判官，見而器之，命子弟與之遊。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi was deputy director of the Pasturage Commission, he saw him and valued him, ordering his sons to associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi served as deputy director of the Pasturage Commission, he took notice of him and held him in esteem, bidding his sons keep his company.

sentences.zh: 擢進士，調須城主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Xucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was made registrar of Xucheng.

sentences.zh: 時河役大興，部役者不得人。

translations.literal: At the time river works were launched on a great scale; the officials in charge of corvée could not manage the laborers.
translations.idiomatic: River works were then launched on a vast scale, and the officials charged with corvée labor could not keep the crews in hand.

sentences.zh: 一夕，噪而潰，因致大獄。

translations.literal: One night they clamored and dispersed, leading to a major prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: One night they raised a clamor and broke apart, which led to a major prosecution.

sentences.zh: 執中往代，終帖然。

translations.literal: Zhizhong went to replace them and in the end all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong went to take their place, and in the end all was quiet.

sentences.zh: 富民賂吏，將創橋所居以罔市利，執中疏其害，使者入吏言使成之，執中曰：「官可去，橋不可創也。」

translations.literal: A wealthy man bribed officials, intending to have a bridge built at his residence to monopolize market profit; Zhizhong memorialized on the harm. The envoy entered and the officials said to make it happen; Zhizhong said: "The official may go, but the bridge must not be built."
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man bribed the clerks, planning to have a bridge built at his residence to corner the market; Zhizhong memorialized on the harm. When the envoy arrived the clerks urged that it be carried through; Zhizhong said, "The official may go, but the bridge shall not be built."

sentences.zh: 卒不能奪。

translations.literal: In the end they could not override him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they could not prevail against him.

sentences.zh: 王安石為政，引執中編修《熙寧條例》，選提舉湖南常平。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held power he brought Zhizhong in to compile the Xining Regulations and selected him as intendant of Hunan Ever-Normal granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi took the reins of government he brought Zhizhong in to compile the Xining Regulations and appointed him intendant of Hunan's Ever-Normal granaries.

sentences.zh: 章惇討五溪，檄執中取大田、離子二峒。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun campaigned against the Five Streams he summoned Zhizhong by dispatch to take the Datian and Lizi passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun campaigned against the Five Streams he issued a dispatch ordering Zhizhong to secure the Datian and Lizi gorges.

sentences.zh: 峒路險絕，期迫，執中但走一校諭其酋，即相率歸命。

translations.literal: The gorge roads were precipitous and inaccessible, the deadline tight; Zhizhong simply sent one sergeant to instruct their chieftains, and they at once came in succession to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The gorge roads were sheer and trackless, the deadline pressing; Zhizhong merely sent one sergeant to address their chieftains, and they at once came in ranks to submit.

sentences.zh: 錄功當遷秩，辭以及父母。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was due for promotion in rank; he declined on the grounds that his parents were still alive.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was entered and he was due for promotion in rank, but he declined while his parents still lived.

sentences.zh: 就徙轉運判官，召為司農丞、提點開封縣鎮。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to transport commissioner and summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and intendant of the county markets of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to transport commissioner and summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and intendant of Kaifeng's county markets.

sentences.zh: 諸縣牧地，民耕歲久，議者將取之，當夷丘墓，伐桑柘，萬家相聚而泣。

translations.literal: In the various counties there was pasture land that the people had farmed for many years; deliberators were about to reclaim it, which would require leveling tombs, felling mulberry and catalpa, and ten thousand households gathered weeping.
translations.idiomatic: In several counties there was pasturage the people had tilled for years; deliberators were about to reclaim it—tombs would be leveled, mulberry and catalpa felled—and ten thousand households gathered, weeping together.

sentences.zh: 執中請於朝，神宗詔復予民。

translations.literal: Zhizhong petitioned the court; Emperor Shenzong ordered it restored to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong petitioned the court, and Emperor Shenzong ordered the land restored to the people.

sentences.zh: 改提點京西北路刑獄。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as judicial intendant for the Northwest circuit around the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned judicial intendant for the Northwest circuit around the capital.

sentences.zh: 時河決廣武，埽危甚，相聚莫敢登。

translations.literal: At the time the Yellow River broke through at Guangwu; the dike-repair works were extremely perilous and the workers gathered but none dared mount them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River then burst its banks at Guangwu; the dike-repair works were desperately perilous, and though the laborers massed together, none dared climb them.

sentences.zh: 執中不顧，立其上，眾隨之如蟻附，不日埽成。

translations.literal: Zhizhong paid no heed, stood upon them, and the crowd followed like ants clinging; within days the works were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong paid no heed, mounted the works and stood upon them; the crowd followed like ants swarming a ridge, and within days the dike was finished.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，為吏部郎中，請選人由縣令、錄事參軍致仕者，升朝籍，得封其親。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was director in the Ministry of Personnel and requested that officials who retired after serving as magistrate or registrar be entered on the court roster and allowed to ennoble their parents.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanyou era he was director in the Ministry of Personnel and asked that officials who retired after serving as county magistrate or registrar be entered on the court roster and permitted to ennoble their parents.

sentences.zh: 兼徐王府侍講、翊善，遷起居舍人、起居郎，權給事中。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as lecturer and tutor to the Prince of Xu's household, was promoted to Attendant Gentleman for Drafting the Imperial Diary and then Recorder of the Sovereign's Movements, and acted as supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as lecturer and tutor in the Prince of Xu's household, was promoted to Attendant Gentleman for Drafting the Imperial Diary and then Recorder of the Sovereign's Movements, and acted as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 有司以天下讞獄失出入者同坐，執中駁之曰：「先王重入而輕出，恤刑之至也。

translations.literal: When the relevant office proposed that throughout the empire those who erred in sentencing—whether too harsh or too lenient—should share punishment equally, Zhizhong objected: "The ancient kings valued adding charges sparingly and releasing lightly—the utmost in compassionate punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the relevant office proposed that throughout the empire officials who erred in sentencing—whether too harsh or too lenient—should share punishment alike, Zhizhong objected, "The ancient kings weighed conviction heavily and acquittal lightly—that is the utmost in compassionate punishment.

sentences.zh: 今一旦均之，恐自是法吏不復肯與生比，非好生洽民之意也。」

translations.literal: Now to make them equal at a stroke—I fear from this legal officials will no longer be willing to weigh toward life; this is not the intent of cherishing life and harmonizing the people."
translations.idiomatic: To equalize them in a single stroke—I fear legal officials will from this refuse to lean toward sparing life; that is not the intent of cherishing life and bringing the people into harmony."

sentences.zh: 進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 邢恕遇赦甄復，執中言：「恕深結蔡確，鼓唱扇搖，今復其官，懼疑中外。」

translations.literal: When Xing Shu was restored to office through amnesty and review, Zhizhong said: "Shu was deeply tied to Cai Que, drumming up and fanning agitation; to restore his office now—I fear it will breed doubt within and without."
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Shu was restored to office through amnesty and review, Zhizhong said, "Shu was deeply bound to Cai Que, drumming up trouble and fanning unrest; to restore him now—I fear it will breed suspicion at court and beyond."

sentences.zh: 遷給事中、刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary and vice minister of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervising secretary and vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，上官均摭執中為呂大防所用，以寶文閣待制知鄆州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, Shangguan Jun gathered charges that Zhizhong had been used by Lü Dafang and had him appointed awaiting-appointment drafter of the Pavilion of Treasured Literature and prefect of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shaosheng era, Shangguan Jun dredged up charges that Zhizhong had served Lü Dafang's faction and had him appointed awaiting-appointment drafter of the Pavilion of Treasured Literature and prefect of Yan.

sentences.zh: 執中寬厚有仁心，屢典刑獄，雪活以百數。

translations.literal: Zhizhong was generous and possessed a humane heart; he repeatedly held judicial posts and cleared or spared lives by the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong was generous of heart and humane in spirit; he repeatedly held judicial posts and cleared or spared lives by the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 明年，夢神人畀以騎都尉，詰旦為客言之，少焉，談笑而逝，年六十三。

translations.literal: The next year he dreamed a divine being bestowed upon him the title Commandant of Cavalry; at dawn he told a guest of it, and shortly thereafter passed away laughing in conversation, age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he dreamed that a divine being bestowed on him the title Commandant of Cavalry; at dawn he told a guest of it, and shortly thereafter passed away mid-conversation and laughter, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋之人才，自祖宗涵養，至於中葉，盛矣。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Song talent, nourished from the founders through the mid-dynasty, flourished abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Song talent, nourished from the founding emperors through the mid-dynasty, had grown abundant indeed.

sentences.zh: 顏復、鄭穆醇然儒者，宜居師表。

translations.literal: Yan Fu and Zheng Mu were pure Confucian scholars, fit to stand as masters and models.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Fu and Zheng Mu were scholars in the purest Confucian mold, fit to stand as masters and models for others.

sentences.zh: 龔鼎臣、喬執中始終不渝厥守，豈易得哉。

translations.literal: Gong Dingchen and Qiao Zhizhong never wavered from their steadfast principles—how easily could such men be found?
translations.idiomatic: Gong Dingchen and Qiao Zhizhong never wavered from the principles they held—men like these, how easily are they found?

sentences.zh: 章衡欲復山後八州，為國啟釁；

translations.literal: Zhang Heng wished to recover the eight prefectures beyond the mountains, opening strife for the state;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng wished to recover the eight prefectures beyond the mountains, opening strife for the realm;

sentences.zh: 孫升以蘇軾比王安石為人；

translations.literal: Sun Sheng compared Su Shi to Wang Anshi in character;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng likened Su Shi to Wang Anshi in character;

sentences.zh: 韓川詆張舜民之言不可行；

translations.literal: Han Chuan denounced Zhang Shunmin's words as impracticable;
translations.idiomatic: Han Chuan denounced Zhang Shunmin's proposals as unworkable;

sentences.zh: 席旦以蔡王見疑，因而擠之。

translations.literal: Xi Dan, seeing Prince Cai under suspicion, pressed him accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Dan, seeing Prince Cai fall under suspicion, pressed him all the harder.

sentences.zh: 然瑕不掩瑜，它善蓋亦有可稱者。

translations.literal: Yet flaws do not obscure jade; their other virtues too surely have something worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a flaw does not obscure the jade; in their other virtues too, surely, there is something worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 古稱「才難不其然」者，其斯之謂歟？

translations.literal: When the ancients said "talent is hard to find—is it not so?" did they not mean precisely this?
translations.idiomatic: When the ancients said that talent is hard to find—is it not exactly this they meant?
